translations.text: And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month: I was among the captives by the river Chebar. And the heavens were opened, and I saw a vision of God.

On the fifth day of the month (this was the fifth year of the captivity of King Jehoiachin) the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chebar.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me,
and I looked, and behold, a lifting wind came from the north, with a great cloud in it, and light all around it, and gleaming fire.
And in its midst there was something like the appearance of the colour of electrum, which is gold, silver and bronze melted together in the midst of the fire, and there was light in it.
And in its midst there was something like the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man,
and each one had four faces, and each one had four wings. Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged. Sparks flashed from them as from gleaming bronze, and their wings were light.
And there was a man's hand beneath their wings on all four of their sides. And the faces of all four of them were…
They did not turn around as they went; each of them went straight ahead, in the direction it faced.
And the likeness of their faces was this: the face of a man; the face of a lion on the right of the four; the face of a calf on the left of the four; and the face of an eagle on the four of them.
And their wings were spread out above on all four of them. Each one had two wings joined to one another, and with two they covered their bodies from above.
And on both sides they went straight ahead, in the direction they faced. Wherever the spirit went, there they also would go, and they did not turn around.
And among the living creatures there was an appearance like burning coals of fire,
like the appearance of torches gathered together among the living creatures, and the brightness of fire, and lightnings came out of the fire.
And I looked, and behold, there was a wheel on the ground near the four living creatures.
And the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of tarshish, and all four of them had one likeness. Their workmanship and their appearance were alike, as if a wheel were inside a wheel.
They went in all four of their directions, and did not turn around as they went.
Nor did their backs turn around, and their height was great. And I saw them, and the backs of all four of them were full of eyes all around.
And when the living creatures went, the wheels also went beside them; when the living creatures rose up from the earth, the wheels also rose up.
And wherever the cloud was, there the spirit would go. The living creatures and the wheels would go, and the wheels would rise up with them, for the spirit of life was in the wheels.
When they went, the wheels went; when they stood, the wheels stood; and when they rose up from the earth, the wheels rose up with them, for the spirit of life was in the wheels.
And above, over the heads of the living creatures, there was the likeness of a firmament, like the appearance of crystal, spread out above their wings.
And beneath the firmament their wings were spread out. They flew one alongside another, and each one's two wings, joined together, covered their bodies.

And I heard the sound of their wings as they went, like the rushing of many waters; like the sound of a multitude as they went, and the sound of their words was like the sound of a great camp. When they stood still, their wings also fell quiet.
And behold, a voice above the firmament that was over their heads.
Like the appearance of a sapphire stone, and the likeness of a throne upon it. And upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness of the form of a man, above it.

And I saw something like the appearance of electrum, which is gold and silver and brass melted together. Such was the radiance from the appearance of his loins upward; and from the appearance of his loins downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its light all around.
Like the appearance of the bow that stands in the clouds on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the radiance around him.

This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. I saw this and fell on my face. And I heard the voice of one speaking, and he said to me: "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you."
And the Spirit came upon me, and lifted me up, and raised me, and set me on my feet, and I heard him as he spoke to me.
And he said to me: "Son of man, I am sending you to the house of Israel, to those who embitter me, who have embittered me, they and their fathers, to this very day.
And say to them: 'Thus says the Lord,'
whether they will listen or be afraid, for it is a house of those who embitter me; and they shall know that you are a prophet among them.

And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, and do not be dismayed before them, for they will provoke you to anger and gather against you all around you, for you dwell among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words, and do not be dismayed at their faces, for it is a house of those who embitter me.
And you shall speak my words to them, whether perhaps they will listen or be afraid, for it is a house of those who embitter me.
And you, son of man, listen to the one speaking to you. Do not become one who embitters, like that house of those who embitter me. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."

And I looked, and behold, a hand stretched out toward me, and in it was a scroll of a book. He unrolled it before me, and there was writing in it on the front, [?], and on the back; written in it were lamentation, misery, and woe.
And he said to me: "Son of man, eat this scroll of this book, and go, and speak to the sons of Israel."
And he opened my mouth, and made me eat the scroll of that book, and he said to me:
"Son of man, let your mouth eat, and let your belly be filled with this scroll of the book that has been given to you." And I ate it, and in my mouth it was sweet as honey.
And he said to me: "Son of man, go, enter the house of Israel, and speak my words to them,
for I am not sending you to a people heavy of tongue; I am sending you to the house of Israel,

nor to many peoples of foreign speech and foreign tongues, nor to those who are hard of tongue, whose speech you do not understand. Even if I were sending you to people like that, they would have listened to you.
But the house of Israel will not listen to you, for they do not want to listen to me, for the whole house of Israel is contentious and hard-hearted."
And behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will make your victory firm against their victory.
And it shall always be stronger than rock. Do not be afraid of them, and do not be dismayed before their faces, for it is a house of embitterers.
And the Lord said to me: Son of man, all the words that I speak to you, take into your heart, and hear them with your ears.
And go, go in to the captives, the sons of your people, and speak and say to them: Thus says the Lord, whether they will listen and desist.
And the Spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great quaking: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place.
And I saw the sound of the wings of the living creatures as they flew one toward another, and the sound of the wheels of their chariot close beside them, and the sound of the quaking.
And the Spirit took me up and lifted me high, and I went on in the vehemence of my spirit. And the hand of the Lord was strong upon me.
And I went in to the captives, lifted up with delight, and I went about among those dwelling by the river Chebar who were there. And I was there seven days, and I lived among them.
And after seven days the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Hear words from my mouth, and warn them from me.

When I say to the lawless man, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not tell him, and do not speak to turn the lawless man away so that he may turn back from his ways and live, that lawless man shall die in his lawlessness, but I will require his blood from your hands.
But if you tell the lawless man, and he does not turn back from his lawlessness and from his evil way, that lawless man shall die in his lawlessness, but you will have saved your own soul.

And if the righteous man turns away from his righteous deeds and commits sin, and I set torment before his face, and he dies because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sins, for his righteous deeds will not be remembered, but I will require his blood from your hands.
If you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he listens and does not sin, the righteous man shall surely live, because you rebuked him, and you will have saved your soul.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he said to me: Arise and go out into the plain, and there my words will be told to you.
And I arose and went out into the plain. And behold, the glory of the Lord was standing there, like the vision and like the glory that I saw by the river Chebar, and I fell on my face.
And the Spirit came upon me and set me up on my feet, and spoke to me and said to me: Go in and shut yourself up inside your house.
And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been put on you, and they will bind you with them, and you will not go out from among them.
And I will bind your tongue, and you will be mute, and you will not be a man who reproves them, for it is a house of embitterers.

And when I speak to you, then I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: whoever hears, let him hear, and whoever is disobedient, let him be disobedient, for it is a house of embitterers.
And you, son of man, take a brick for yourself and set it before your face, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.
And lay siege around it, and build bulwarks [?] against it, and bring an army up against it, and set camps against it, and post archers around it.

And you, take for yourself an iron griddle, and set it up for yourself as an iron wall between you and the city, and set your face toward it. And it shall be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.

And you shall lie on your left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of the one hundred and ninety days that you lie on it. You shall bear their iniquities.
And I have given you their two iniquities as a number of one hundred and ninety days. And you shall bear the iniquities of the house of Israel.
And you shall complete these, and you shall lie on your right side. And you shall bear the iniquities of the house of Judah for forty days; I have appointed for you a day for each year,
and for the siege of Jerusalem. Set your face, and strengthen your arm against it, and prophesy against it.
Behold, I have put bonds on you. And do not turn from one side to the other until the days of your siege are completed.

And you, take for yourself wheat and barley, and beans and lentils, and millet and spelt, and put them into an earthen vessel, and make them into bread for yourself according to the number of the days that you lie on your side. For one hundred and ninety days you shall eat it.
And the food that you eat, you shall eat by weight: twenty shekels a day. You shall eat it at set times.
You shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin. You shall drink it at set times.
And you shall eat it as a barley cake. You shall bake it in human dung before their eyes.
And say to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: In this way the sons of Israel shall eat unclean food among the nations.

And I said: By no means, O Lord God of Israel! My soul has never been defiled with anything unclean. From my birth until now I have not eaten anything that died of itself or was torn by wild beasts, and no foul flesh has ever entered my mouth.
And the Lord said to me: Behold, I have given you cattle dung in place of human dung, and you shall make your bread on it.
And the Lord said to me: Son of man, behold, I will break the strength of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and in want, and they shall drink water by measure and in ruin,
so that they will lack bread and water, and a man and his brother will be ruined, and they will waste away in their iniquities.
And you, son of man, take for yourself a sword sharper than a barber's razor, and get it for yourself. And pass it over your head and your beard, and take a pair of scales and weigh the hair.

And you shall burn a fourth part of it with fire in the midst of the city when the days of your siege are completed. And take a fourth of it and burn it in its midst; and cut a fourth of it with the sword all around it; and scatter a fourth of it to every wind. And I will send a sword after them.
And take from there a few in number, and wrap them in your garment.
And take some of these again, and throw them into the midst of the fire, and burn them with fire, and fire shall come out from it. And say to all the house of Israel:
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: This is Jerusalem. I have set it in the midst of the nations, with the lands around it.
And tell my judgment to that lawless one among the nations, and my law to the lands around her, for they have cast my judgments far away and have not walked in my law.

Therefore thus says Adonai, the Lord, the Lord: Because your cause comes from the nations that are around you, and you have not walked in my law and have not kept my judgments, and have not even walked according to the judgments of the nations that were around you;
therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you,
and I will carry out judgment in your midst before the nations, and I will do in your midst what I have not done, and I will never again do anything like it, because of your abominations.
Therefore fathers will eat their children in your midst, and children will eat their fathers, and I will carry out judgment in your midst, and I will scatter all your remnant to every wind.

Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, the Lord, because you have defiled my holiness with all your abominations, I too will cast you away. My eye will no longer spare you, and I will not have mercy on you.

A fourth part of you will be wiped out by death, and a fourth of it will be consumed by famine in your midst. And a fourth of you I will scatter to every wind, and a fourth of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw the sword after them.
And my anger and my wrath against them will be spent. And you will understand that I, the Lord, have spoken in my jealousy, so that I may bring my wrath against them to its end.
And I will make you a desolation, and your daughters around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.
And you will be an object of groaning and grief among the nations around you, when I carry out judgment upon you in vengeance, in my anger. I, the Lord, have spoken.
When I send out the arrows of famine against them, there will be want in your midst, and I will break the strength of your bread in your midst.
And I will send famine and evil beasts among you, and I will torment you, and death and famine will pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you all around you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face firmly toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them, and say:

Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to the mountains and valleys, and to the hills and ravines: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and your high places will be destroyed.
And your altars and your shrines will be smashed, and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
And I will scatter your bones around your altars,
in all your dwelling places. The cities will be laid waste and the high places will be ruined, so that I may destroy your altars, and your idols will be smashed, and your shrines will be laid waste.
And the slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
When some of you have escaped my sword among the nations, and when you have been scattered among the lands,

then those of you who have escaped will remember me among the nations where they were taken captive. For I have sworn against their heart that turned away from me, and against their eyes that went whoring after the track of their ways. And they will strike their faces for the wickedness they committed in all their abominations.
And they will understand that I am the Lord; I, the Lord, have spoken.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Clap with your hand and stamp with your foot, and say: Aha, over all the abominations of the house of Israel! By sword and by death and by famine they shall fall.
The one who is near shall fall by death, and the one who is far off shall be finished by death, and the one who is besieged shall perish by famine; and I will carry out my wrath upon them,

and you shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain lie among your idols around your altars, on every high hill and under every shady tree, where they offered a fragrant smell of sweet odour to their idols.

And I will stretch out my hand against them, and I will make the land a place of ruin and destruction, from the wilderness of Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and you shall know that I am the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
And you, son of man, say: Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to the land of Israel: The end is coming upon the four corners of the land,
the end is coming upon you,
you who dwell in the land. The time is coming, the day has drawn near, not with tumult and not with pangs.
Now very soon I will pour out my wrath upon you, and I will carry out my anger among you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye shall not spare you, and I will not have pity on you. For I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord who strikes.
Now the end is coming to you, and I will send it upon you, and I will take vengeance for your ways, and I will bring your abominations upon you.
My eye shall not spare you, and I will not have pity on you, for I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord:
Behold, the end is coming. Behold, the day of the Lord, and the rod has blossomed; insolence has risen up.
And I will shatter the strength of the lawless, and not with tumult and not with haste;
the time is coming. Behold, the day: let the one who buys not rejoice, and let the one who sells not lament,
for the one who buys shall no longer return to the seller, and no man shall keep hold of his own life before his eyes.
Blow the trumpet, and carry out judgment in full.
War and sword outside, death and famine inside. Whoever is out in the field shall be finished by the sword, and those who are in the city shall be consumed by famine and death.
And if any of them escape and get away and are in the mountains, I will slay them all, each one in his falsehood.
All hands shall go slack, and all thighs shall be defiled with wetness.
And they shall put on sackcloth, and dismay shall cover them, and shame shall be on every face among them, and baldness on every head.

Their silver shall be scattered in the streets, and their gold shall be held in contempt. Their souls shall not be satisfied, and their bellies shall not be filled, for the punishment of their falsehoods has come upon them.

The choicest of their ornaments they set up for pride, and they made images of their abominations from them. Therefore I have given it back to them as uncleanness, and I will hand them over to uncleanness,
and I will hand them over into the hands of strangers to be plundered, and to the vile of the earth as captives, so that they may defile them.
And I will turn my face away from them, and they will defile my watching-place. And they will go into it unguarded, and they will defile them,
and they will make defilement, for the land is filled with blood of judgment, and the city is full of lawlessness.
And I will turn away the multitude of their strength, and their holy place will be defiled.
Relief will come, and they will seek peace, and there will be none,
and rumour will come upon rumour, and woe upon woe, and a vision will be sought from the prophet, and the law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The ruler will clothe himself in ruin, and the hands of the people of the land will grow weak. I will deal with them according to their ways, and by their own judgments I will take vengeance on them, and they will know that I am the Lord.
And it came to pass in the sixth year, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Israel were sitting before me. And the hand of the Lord came upon me,
and I looked, and behold, the likeness of a man: from his loins downward, fire; and from his loins upward, it looked like gold and silver and bronze melted together; such was its colour.

And the likeness of a hand stretched out and took me by a lock of my head, and the spirit lifted me up between heaven and earth and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, before the gates of the court that faces north, where the pillar of the purchaser stood.
And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, like the vision I had seen in the plain.
And he said to me: Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north. And I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and behold, from the north toward the gate on the side of the sunrise.
And he said to me: Son of man, do you see what these are doing? Great lawlessness these men commit here, so that they are driven far from my holy places; and you will see yet [?] greater lawlessness.
And he brought me in before the gate of the court,
and he said to me: Son of man, dig. And I dug, and behold, a door.
And he said to me: Go in and see the lawless deeds that these men commit here.
And I went in and looked, and behold, vain abominations, and all the idols of the house of Israel portrayed on it all around.

And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jechoniah son of Shaphan standing among them, stood before them, and each of them had a censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense was rising.

And the Lord said to me: Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing, each in his own secret chamber? For they have said: The Lord does not see; the Lord has forsaken the land.
And he said to me: You will see yet greater lawless deeds that these men commit.
And he brought me in before the gate of the house of the Lord that faces north, and behold, women were sitting there, mourning for Tammuz.
And he said to me: Son of man, do you see? And again you will see other deeds greater than these.

And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord, before the doors of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, where there were about twenty men. Their backs were turned toward the temple of the Lord and their faces the other way, and they were worshipping the sun.

And he said to me: Have you seen, son of man? Is it a small thing for the house of Judah to commit the lawlessness that they commit here? For they have filled the land with lawlessness, and behold, they are like people who show contempt.
And I will deal with them in wrath; my eye will not spare, and I will not have pity.
And he cried in my ears with a loud voice and said: The vengeance on the city has drawn near. And each of them had a weapon of destruction in his hand.

And behold, six men were coming from the way of the upper gate that faces north, and each man had an axe in his hand. And one man among them was clothed in a robe reaching to the feet, with a sapphire sash at his waist. And they went in and stood near the bronze altar.

And the glory of the Lord God of Israel went up from the cherubim that it had been upon, to the open court of the temple's sanctuary. And he called the man who was clothed in the robe reaching to the feet, who had the sash fastened around his waist,
and said to him: Go through the middle of Jerusalem and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and grieve over all the lawless deeds that are done among them.
And to these others he said in my hearing: Go into the city after him and strike. Let your eye not spare, and do not have pity.

Kill old man and young man, infant and virgin and woman, until they are wiped out. But do not touch anyone who has the mark on him. And begin with my holy places. And they began with the elders who were inside the house.
He said to them: Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead. Go out and kill.
And while they were killing, I fell on my face and cried out and said: Woe is me, woe is me, Lord, Lord! Will you wipe out the remnant of Israel as you pour out your wrath on Jerusalem?

And he said to me: The falsehoods of the house of Israel and of Judah have grown very great indeed, for the land is filled with many peoples, and the city is full of falsehood and uncleanness. For they say: The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not see.
So my eye will not spare, and I will not have pity. I will bring their ways down on their own heads.
And behold, the man who was clothed in the long robe (podērēs) and had the sash fastened around his waist answered and said: I have done as you commanded me.
And I looked, and behold, on the firmament that was above the head of the cherub there was something like a sapphire stone, in the likeness of a throne, above them.

And he said to the man who was clothed in the robe: Go in between the wheels that are beneath the cherubim, and fill your hands [?] with burning coals from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city. And he went in before my eyes.
And the cherub stood on the right side of the temple when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
And the glory of the Lord rose up from the cherubim to the open court of the temple. And the cloud filled the house, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord.
And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the inner court, like the voice of God Shaddai when he speaks.

And it came to pass, as he was commanding the man who was clothed in the holy garment, he said to him: "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim." And he went in and stood beside the wheels.
And he stretched out his hand into the fire that was in the midst of the cherubim, and took some and put it into the hands of the man who was clothed in the holy garment. And he took it and went out.
And I saw the cherubim, and the likeness of a man's hands under their wings.
And I looked, and behold, four wheels stood beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub, and the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of carbuncle stone.
And all four of them looked alike, as if a wheel were within a wheel.

And when they moved, they went in any of the four directions. They did not turn around as they went, for they went to whatever place the first, the one side, faced, and they did not turn around as they went.
Their backs, their hands and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around all four wheels.
And the wheels were called "Gelgel," as I heard.
And these cherubim were the living creatures that I saw by the river Chebar.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved too, and they stayed beside them. And when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise up from the earth, the wheels did not turn away from them.
When they stood still, the wheels stood still, and when the cherubim rose up, the wheels also rose up with them, for the spirit of life was with them.
And the glory of the Lord went out from the temple and mounted upon the cherubim.

And the cherubim lifted up their wings and rose up from the earth before me as they went out, and the wheels beside them. They stood at the doorway of the gate of the house of the Lord, at the front [?], and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above.
These are the living creatures that I saw beneath the God of Israel by the river Chebar, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each one had four faces, and the likeness of a man's hands was beneath their wings.
And the appearance of their faces: these are the faces that I saw beneath the glory of the God of Israel by the river Chebar. And each of them went straight forward.

And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the gate of the house of the Lord that faces east. And behold, at the doorway of the court there were about twenty-five men, and among them I saw Jechoniah son of Iezer, and Pelatiah of Benaiah, son of Saphan, leaders of the people.
And the Lord said to me: "Son of man, these are the men who devise vanity and plot evil plans in this city,
and they say: 'Have not the houses been newly built just now? This city is the cauldron, and we are the meat.'
Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, son of man."
And the Spirit fell upon me and said to me: "Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Say this to the house of Israel: I know the thoughts of your heart.
You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled its streets with the wounded."
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Your dead, whom you have slain in its midst, these are the flesh, and this city is the cauldron [?]; and I will bring you out of its midst.
You fear the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, says the Lord, the Lord.
And I will bring you out of its midst, and I will give you into the hands of foreigners, and I will execute judgment among you.
You shall fall by the sword; on the mountains of Israel I will judge you, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
It shall not be a cauldron [?] for you, and you shall not be flesh within it; on the mountains of Israel I will judge you,
and you shall know that I am the Lord.

And it came to pass, while I was prophesying, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice, and said: Woe is me, O Lord, Lord! You are making an end of the remnant of Israel.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:

Son of man, your brothers, and the men of your captivity, and all the house of Israel have been brought to an end, those to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: You have been put far away from the Lord; to us the land has been given as an inheritance. Therefore say to them:
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I have driven them far off among the nations and scattered them over all the earth, and I will be to them a small sanctuary in the lands into which they have gone.
Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the lands among which I scattered them, and I will give them the land of Israel.
And they shall enter there and take away from it their abominations and all its iniquities.
And I will give them another heart, and I will give them a new spirit, and I will tear the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk in my commandments and keep my judgments and do them; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
And as for those who walked after the heart of their abominations and their iniquities, as their heart led them, I will bring their ways upon their own heads, says the Lord, the Lord.
And the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them, above them.
And the glory of the Lord rose up from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain that was before the city.
And the Spirit took me up and brought me to the land of the Chaldeans, to the captives, in a vision by the Spirit of God. And I came up out of the vision that I had seen,
and I spoke to the captives all the words of the Lord that he had shown me.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said to me:
Son of man, you dwell in the midst of their falsehoods; they have eyes to see and do not see, and they have ears to hear and do not hear, for it is a house of those who provoke [me].

And you, son of man, make for yourself baggage for captivity by day before them, and you shall be carried captive from your place to another place before them, so that they may see, for it is a house of those who provoke [me].
And you shall bring out your baggage, baggage for captivity, by day before their eyes, and you shall go out in the evening as a captive goes out.
Before them break through the wall for yourself, and go out through it.
You shall be lifted up on a shoulder before them, and go out secretly. You shall cover your face and not see the land, for I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.

And I did as the Lord commanded me, according to all his word. I brought out the baggage of captivity by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall by myself, and went out secretly; I was lifted up on a shoulder before them.
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, in the morning, and said to me:
Son of man, was it not said to you that the house of Israel is a house of rebellious people who provoke me? They say to you, 'What is this you are doing?'
Say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to the ruler and leader of Jerusalem and of all the people of Israel who are in its midst.
Say to them: I am making signs. As I have done as a figure, so it shall be done among them: they shall go into exile and captivity.

And the ruler among them shall be carried off on the shoulder [?], and shall go out secretly through the wall, and shall dig through it to go out. For this reason he shall cover his face, so that he does not see with his eye, and he shall not see the land.
And I will spread my snare over him, and he shall be caught in my encirclement. And I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans; but he shall not see it, and there he shall die.
And all those around him, and all his helpers, and all his [?] I will scatter to every wind. And I will draw the sword after them,
and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I scatter them among the nations and sow them throughout the lands.

And I will leave a few men of them, few in number, from the sword, from death and from famine, so that they may tell of all their iniquities among the nations to which they go, and they shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, eat your bread with grief, and drink your water with distress and torment.

And say to the people of the land: Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread in want, and drink their water in ruin, so that the land may be destroyed together with all that fills it, for all who dwell in it live in ungodliness.
And the cities that are inhabited in it shall be laid waste, and the land shall be given over to ruin, and they shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, what is this proverb of yours in the land of Israel, in which you say, 'The days are far off, and the visions have come to nothing'?

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will overturn that proverb, and the house of Israel shall no longer use that proverb. Instead, say to them: The days have drawn near, and the words of every vision.
For there shall no longer be any false vision or divination for flattery among the sons of Israel.

For thus says the Lord: I will speak my words; I will speak and I will act, and I will not delay any longer. For in your days, O house of rebels, I will speak a word and do it, says the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, see, the house of Israel, which rebels against me, is talking, and they say: 'The vision that this man sees is for many days and distant times; he is prophesying about these.'
Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: None of my words that I have spoken shall be delayed any longer; I will do it soon and quickly, says the Lord Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, prophesy, and say to them: Hear the word of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord Lord: Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and see nothing at all!
Your prophets, O Israel, are like foxes in the desert.
They did not set things up firmly, and they gathered the flock for the house of Israel. Those who were saying "On the day of the Lord" did not rise up,
those who saw falsehood and practised vain divination; those who say, "Says the Lord," when the Lord did not send them, and they began to try to establish their word.
Did you not see a word of falsehood, and speak vain divination?
Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord Lord: Because your words are falsehood and your divinations are vain, therefore, behold, I am against you, says the Lord.

And I will stretch out my hand against those prophets who see falsehood and speak vanity. They shall not be in the instruction of my people, nor shall they be written in the book of the house of Israel, and they shall not enter the land of Israel; and they shall know that I am the Lord.
Because they led my people astray, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace. This one builds a wall, and these plaster it. Will it fall?

Say to those who plaster it that it shall fall. There shall be a sweeping, destructive rain, and I will bring stones of hard rock against its fastenings, and it shall fall; and there shall be a wind that lifts it up, and it shall be torn apart.
And behold, the wall has fallen. Will they not say to you, "Where is that plaster of yours with which you plastered it?"

Therefore thus says the Lord Lord: I will strike with a wind that lifts up, in wrath; and a destructive rain shall come in my anger; and I will send stones of hard rock upon them in my anger, to destroy them.

And I will tear down the wall that you plastered, and it shall fall. And I will lay it on the ground, and its foundation shall be laid bare. It shall fall and be brought to an end with reproof, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
And I will carry out my wrath upon that wall and upon those who plastered it, and it shall fall; and I said to you: The wall is no more, and neither are those who plastered it.
The prophets of Israel, who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and who see peace for it, when there shall be no peace, says the Lord Lord.
And you, son of man, set your face firmly against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart. Prophesy against them,

and say: Thus says the Lord Lord: Woe to those who sew pillows under every elbow of the arm, and who make coverings for every head of every age, to turn souls aside! The souls of my people were turned aside, and they kept souls alive for themselves,

and they profaned me before my people for a handful of barley and a morsel of bread, to kill souls that were not meant to die and to keep alive souls that were not meant to live, while you speak to a people that listens to vain words.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I am against your pillows, where you gather souls, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will send away their souls to be scattered.
And I will tear your coverings [?], and I will deliver my people from your hands, and they shall no longer be in your hands to be gathered; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

Because you perverted the soul of the righteous, though I did not pervert it, and you strengthened the hands of the lawless, so that he would by no means turn back from his evil way, that he might live.
Therefore you shall not see falsehood, and you shall not practise divination; and I will deliver my people from your hands, and you shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And men from the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, these men have set their thoughts in their hearts, and they have set the punishment of their falsehoods before their faces. Shall I indeed answer, and shall I give them a word in reply?

Therefore speak to them and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Any man of the house of Israel who has set his thoughts in his heart, and sets the punishment of his falsehood before his face, and comes to the prophet, I the Lord will answer him a word in those things by which his mind is held captive,
so that he may make the house of Israel go astray according to their heart, which has become estranged from me through their thoughts.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Turn back, and turn away from your deeds and from all your ungodliness, and turn your faces back.

For any man of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners who sojourn in Israel, who becomes estranged from me, and sets his thoughts in his heart, and sets the punishment of his falsehood before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of him through me, I the Lord will answer him in that by which he is held captive.
And I will set my face firmly against that man, and I will make him a desolation and a ruin, and I will remove him from among my people; and you shall know that I am the Lord.
And if the prophet goes astray and speaks, I the Lord have led that prophet astray, and I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
And they shall bear their iniquities: according to the iniquity of the one who inquires, so in the same way, according to that iniquity, it shall be to the prophet,

so that the house of Israel may no longer go astray from me, and that they may no longer defile themselves with their sins. And they shall be my people, and I will be their God, says the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, if a land sins against me by committing a transgression, I will stretch out my hand against it, and break its supply of bread, and send famine, and wipe out from it both man and beast.
And if these three men were in it, Noah, Job and Daniel, they would be saved by their righteousness, says the Lord Almighty.
Or if I bring evil beasts upon it and torment that land, and it becomes a ruin, and no one passes through it because of the beasts,
If these three men were in its midst, as I live, says the Lord, the Lord, whether sons or daughters [?], they alone would escape, but that land would be given over to destruction.
Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, "Let a sword go through that land," and I take away from it both people and livestock,
and these three men were in its midst, as I live, says the Lord, they could not deliver sons or daughters; they alone would escape.
Or if I send death upon that land and pour out my wrath upon it with blood, to wipe out from it both people and livestock,
and Noah and Job and Daniel were in its midst, as I live, says the Lord, sons or daughters alone would be left [?], but they by their righteousness would deliver their own souls.
Thus says the Lord: If I send these four evil punishments of mine, the sword and famine and the evil beast and death, upon Jerusalem, to destroy from it both people and livestock,

and there are survivors left in it who have escaped from it, and they bring out sons or daughters from there, behold, they will come out to you, and you will see their ways and their thoughts, and you will feel regret over the evils that I called down upon Jerusalem, all the evil that I brought upon it.
And they will plead with you, for you will see their ways and their thoughts, and you will know that it was not in vain that I called down upon it what I did to it, says the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
"And you, son of man, what will become [?] of the wood of the vine, out of all the wood of the branches that are among the trees of the forest?
Will they take wood from it to make anything useful? Will they take a peg [?] from it to hang every kind of vessel on it?
It is only fit to be given to the fire to be burned. Year by year [?] its prunings are consumed by the fire, and it is completely used up. Surely it cannot be of use for any work.
Even when it is whole, it is not fit for any work, much less once the fire has completely consumed it; then it is no longer of any use.

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: As with the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire to be burned, so I will give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And I will set my face against them. They will come out of the fire, and the fire will consume them. And they will know that I am the Lord when I set my face firmly against them.
And I will give their land over to ruin, because they fell into sins, says the Lord, the Lord."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
"Son of man, bear witness to Jerusalem about her lawless deeds,
and say to her: Thus says the Lord God of Israel to Jerusalem: Your root and your birth are from Canaan. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.
And at your birth, on the day you were born, your navel cord was not cut, you were not washed with water, you were not rubbed with salt, and you were not wrapped in swaddling cloths.

Nor did my eye pity you, so as to do even one of these things for you, to give [?] anything of mine for you, and you were thrown out onto the open field because of the loathing [?] of your soul, on the day that you were born.
And I passed by you and saw you defiled in your own blood, and I said to you: From your blood comes your life.

"Multiply!" As the sprouting of the field I gave you, and you multiplied and grew great, and entered into the cities of cities. Your breasts rose up, and your hair sprouted, but you were naked and shameful.

And I passed by you and saw you, and behold, your time was the time of those who come to lodge [?], and I spread my wings over you and covered your shame, and I swore to you and entered into a covenant with you, says the Lord Lord. And you became mine,
and I washed you with water and washed your blood away from you, and anointed you with oil.
And I clothed you in many-colored garments, and shod your feet with hyacinth-blue, and girded you with fine linen, and clothed you with embroidered work.
And I adorned you with ornaments, and put bracelets on your hands and a necklace on your neck.
And I put on you an earring, and rings on your ears, and a crown of glory on your head.
And you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, embroidered work and many colors. You ate fine flour and oil and honey, and you became exceedingly beautiful.
And the fame of your beauty went out among the nations, for it was made perfect in comeliness and splendor, which I set upon you, says the Lord Lord.
But you trusted in your beauty, and played the harlot by your name, and poured out your harlotry on everyone who passed by on the road.
And you took some of your garments and made for yourself stitched idols, and played the harlot with them; and you shall not enter, nor shall it be.
And you took the vessels of your glory, of the gold and of my silver which I gave you, and made for yourself images of a male [?], and played the harlot with them.
And you took some of your many-colored garments and clothed them with them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
And my bread which I gave you (I fed you fine flour and oil and honey), you set it before them as a sweet-smelling fragrance; and so it was, says the Lord Lord.
And you took your sons and your daughters whom you bore, and slaughtered them to the idols to be devoured, as though it were a small thing [?] that you played the harlot.
And you slaughtered your children and gave them over as [?] an offering of turning-away for yourself to them.
This was beyond all your harlotries; and you did not remember your infancy, the day when you were naked and shameful. Defiled in your own blood you lived,
and you were with all your wickedness, says the Lord, and you built for yourself a house of harlotry.
And you made for yourself a public display [?], like a marketplace, in all the streets.
And at the head of every way out you built your brothels, and you defiled your beauty, and spread your thighs to everyone who passed by on the road, and multiplied your harlotries.
And you played the harlot with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, great of body, and many times you played the harlot to provoke me to anger.

And I will stretch out my hand over you and take away your ordinances, and give you over to the souls of those who hate you, the daughters of foreigners, who turned you aside from your way; and you became ungodly.
And you played the harlot with the daughters of the Assyrians, and not even so were you satisfied; you played the harlot and were not satisfied.
And you multiplied your covenants toward the land of the Canaanites and the Chaldeans; and not even with these were you satisfied.
What shall I promise [?] to your daughter, says the Lord Lord? For you did all these things of a harlot woman, threefold among your daughters.
You built your places of fornication at the head of every road, and you made your way through every street; and you became like a harlot who gathers payment.
An adulterous woman is like you, who takes payment from her own husband.
To all her fornicators she would, in turn, give payment. And you gave payment to all your lovers, and you loaded them with burdens to come to you from all around in your fornication;
and in your fornication perversity came about in you more than in other women. No one fornicated as you did, for you added payment and no payment was given to you, and perversity came about in you.
Therefore, harlot, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because you poured out your bronze, and your shame was revealed by your fornication with your lovers and with all your schemes, and by the blood of your children, which you gave to them,

therefore, behold, I will gather against you all your lovers, among whom you mingled, and all whom you loved, together with those whom you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, and I will reveal your wickedness before them, and they will see all your shame.
And I will take from you the vengeance due to an adulteress, and I will set you in the blood of wrath and of jealousy.

And I will give you into their hands, and they will destroy your place of fornication and tear down your foundation. They will strip your clothing from you, take from you the vessel of your boasting, and leave you naked and shamed.
And they will bring peoples against you and heap stones upon you, and they will cut you down with their swords.
And they will burn your houses with fire and carry out vengeance on you before many women. And I will turn you back from your fornication, and you will no longer give payment.
And I will pour out my anger on you, and I will carry out my jealousy against you. Then I will be at rest and will be troubled no longer.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth, and you provoked me with all this, behold, I have brought your ways down upon your own head, says the Lord, the Lord. This is how you committed ungodliness along with all your lawless deeds.
This is everything that they have spoken about you as a proverb. And they will say: "As the mother,

so also the daughter." You are the daughter of the mother who rejected her husband and her children, and [the sister] of your sisters who rejected their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
And your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters, who live on your left. And your younger sister, who lives on your right, is Sodom and her daughters.
Yet you did not merely walk in their ways, nor did you do only a little according to their lawless deeds; you went far beyond them in your ways.
As I live, says the Lord, the Lord, Sodom and her daughters did not do as you and your daughters have done.

But this was the lawlessness of the Sodomites, of your sister: pride, with plenty of bread and an abundance of her luxuries, and of her daughters. She and her daughters had this, and they did not hold out a hand to the needy and the poor,
and they were very haughty and committed lawlessness before me, and I took them away, as you saw.
And Samaria did not commit half of your sins. You multiplied lawlessness more than she did, and you made your sisters appear righteous by all the lawlessness that you committed.

So bear your punishment, because you corrupted your sisters by your lawlessness. You acted more lawlessly than they did, and you made them appear more righteous than yourself. You were put to shame; so bear your disgrace for making your sisters appear righteous.
And I will bring back their captivity: the captivity of Sodom and her daughters. I will bring back the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and I will bring back your captivity among them,
so that you may bear your punishment and be disgraced by everyone, for all that you did to provoke me to anger.

And your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they were at first. And Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were at first. And you and your daughters will be restored too, as you were at first.
And if only Sodom your sister had been in your hearing and in your mouth in the days of your arrogance,
before your wickedness was revealed, as now you are a reproach to the daughters of Assyria and to all those around her, to the daughters of the foreigners who are near you on every side!
You have borne your impieties and your lawless deeds, says the Lord, the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: I will do to you as you have done. For you showed contempt by transgressing my covenant, which was made with you.
[?] in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant for you.
And you will remember your ways and be put to shame when you receive your sisters of foreign descent. I will give them to you to build up, but not by virtue of your covenant.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord,
so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I show you mercy for all that you have done, says the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, tell a story and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: A great eagle, with great wings and a long body, full of talons, which intended to go into Lebanon, took its choice fir trees.
He cut off the tips of its young growth, carried them away to the land of Canaan, and set them in a walled city.
And he took some of the seed of the land and put it in a plain as a plant beside many waters. He set it up for watering [?].
And it sprouted and became a vine, weak and small in size to look at, with its branches above him and its roots beneath him. And it became a vine, put out shoots [?], and spread out its tendrils [?].

And there was another great eagle, with great wings and many talons. And behold, that vine had wound itself around him, with its roots toward him, and it sent out its branches toward him, so that he might be with the clod [?] of its planting,
in a good field beside many waters [?] it, so that it might put out shoots [?], bring forth young growth, bear fruit, and become a great vine.

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: If it prospers, will not the roots of its tenderness and its fruit rot, and all its first growth wither? And not with a great arm, nor with many people, did they pull it up by its roots.
And behold, it grows fat. Will it prosper? Will it not wither when the fiery wind blows on it?
And the word of the Lord came to me and said to me:

Son of man, say to that rebellious house: Do you not know what this is? Say to them: When the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, and takes away its king and its princes, and brings them with him to Babylon,
and he takes one of the royal seed, and makes a covenant with him, and brings him under a curse. And he took away the leaders of the land,
so that they might make the kingdom altogether weak, so that they might not be exalted, and so that they might keep his covenant and uphold it.

And he rebelled against him and sent his messengers to Egypt, so that they might give him horses and many people. Will he prosper, or will he escape, he who rebelled and broke the covenant? Will he escape?

As I live, says the Lord, the Lord: surely in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, that covenant of mine which I made with him, in Babylon he shall die.
And Pharaoh will not wage war with him with great strength or with many people, by bringing up an army and by building siege-ramparts for arrows, to take the lives of men.
And he despised the oath and broke the covenant. And behold, he gave his hand, and did all these things to him; he shall not escape.
Therefore say: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: As I live, surely because he despised my oath, and because of my covenant which he broke, for this I will repay it on his head.
And I will spread out my net, and he shall be caught in its encirclement.
With all his ranks they shall fall by the sword, and I will scatter their remnant to every wind, and you shall know that I am the Lord who has spoken.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I myself will take from the cedars; I will cut off from the top of their heart, and I will plant it on a high mountain,

and I will hang it up; on the lofty mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it shall bring forth shoots and fruit. And it shall become a great cedar, and all the birds shall rest under it, and all the beasts of the field shall rest under its shade, and its branches shall be restored.

And all the trees of the field shall know that I am the Lord, who brought low the high tree and raised up the low tree, and dried up the green tree, and made the dry tree sprout. I the Lord have spoken, and I will do it.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
Son of man, what is this proverb of yours among the sons of Israel, which they say: The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth were set on edge?
As I live, says the Lord, from now on this proverb shall no longer be a saying in Israel.
For all souls are mine: as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul that sins, it shall die.
But a man who is righteous, who does righteousness,

He does not eat upon the mountains, and does not let his eyes go after the desires of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbour's wife, and he does not touch a woman while she is in her menstrual impurity.
He does not oppress anyone, and he returns the pledge to the debtor, and he does not seize plunder. He gives his bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked.
He does not lend his silver at interest, and he does not take increase. He turns his hand away from falsehood. And he judges righteously between a man and his neighbour.
He is perfect in my commandments, and he keeps my ordinances so as to do them. Such a man is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord, the Lord.
And if he begets a son who is vile, a shedder of blood and a doer of sin,
and who does not walk in the way of his righteous father, but has eaten upon the mountains, and has defiled his neighbour's wife,
and has oppressed the helpless and the poor, and has seized plunder, and has not given back the pledge, and has lifted his eyes to idols, and has committed lawlessness,
and has lent silver at usury and taken increase: this man shall not live, for he has done all these lawless things. He shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.

If he begets a son, and the son sees all the sins that his father has committed, and is afraid, and does not do likewise: 15 he has not eaten upon the mountains, and has not lifted his eyes to the desires of the house of Israel, and has not defiled his neighbour's wife,
and has not oppressed anyone; he has not taken a pledge, and has not seized plunder; he has given his bread to the hungry, and has clothed the naked,

and has turned his hand away from falsehood; he has not taken usury or increase, and he has done righteousness, and has walked in my commandments: this man shall not die for the sin of his father, but he shall surely live.
If his father has afflicted anyone, and has seized plunder, and has done evil among my people, such a man shall die in his own falsehood.
And you say, “Why is it that the son has not borne the sin of the father?” Because the son has done righteousness, and has kept all my law and done it. This man shall surely live.

The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the sin of the father, nor shall the father bear the sin of his son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the lawlessness of the lawless shall be upon himself.
And if the lawless man turns away from all the lawless things he has done, and from then on keeps all my commandments, and does righteousness and mercy, he shall surely live, and shall not die.
None of all the sins he has committed shall be remembered. By the righteousness that he has done, by that he shall live.
I have not willingly desired the death of the sinner, says the Lord, the Lord, but rather that he should turn from his evil way, and live.

If, on the other hand, the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and does evil according to all the lawlessness that the lawless man has done, none of the righteous deeds he has done shall be remembered. He shall die in the transgression he has committed and in the sins he has sinned.
And you have said, “The way of the Lord is not right.” Now hear, O house of Israel: is it my way that is not right? Or is it not your way, rather than mine, that is not right?
If a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits sin, and dies in the sin that he committed, in it he shall die.
And if the lawless man turns away from the lawlessness that he committed, and does judgment and righteousness, he has preserved his soul,
and he has turned away from all the ungodly deeds that he committed; he shall surely live, and he shall not die.
And the sons of Israel say, "The way of the Lord is not right." Is my way not right? No, it is your way that is not right, O house of Israel.
I will judge each one of you according to your ways, O house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back, and turn away from all your lawless deeds, and you shall not become a torment of falsehood.

Turn back of your own accord, and cast away from you all your lawless deeds, the lawless deeds that you have committed against me, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why will you perish, O house of Israel?
For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord, the Lord.
And you, son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Israel,
and say to him: Why did your mother feed like a whelp among lions, and among lions multiply her whelps?
And he sprang out [?] toward the whelps, became a lion, and learned to seize prey; he devoured men.
And the nations heard of him; he was caught in their pit of corruption, and they led him with a hook to Egypt.
And they saw that he had gone away from her, and his strength had perished. And she brought another of her whelps and set him up as a lion.
And he went about among the lions, became a lion, and learned to seize prey; he devoured men.
And he fed in his boldness, and he laid waste their cities, and he ruined the land and all that fills it with the sound of his roaring.
And the nations from the surrounding countries set upon him, and spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit of corruption.
And they put him in a hook and a cage; he came to the king of the Babylonians, and they put him in prison, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine, like a pomegranate blossom planted by the waters; its growth and its fruit came from many waters.
And it had a rod over the tribes of the leaders, and it was raised high in its greatness among the trees, and it saw its own beauty in the multitude of its branches.
But it was broken down in wrath and fell to the ground, and the hot wind dried up its branches, and vengeance was taken on them, and its strong rod withered, and fire consumed it.
And now they have planted it in the wilderness, in a waterless land.
And fire went out from the rod of its chosen branches and devoured it, and there was no strong rod left in it, no tribe [?]. This is a parable of lament, and it shall be for a lamentation.
And in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, some of the elders of the house of Israel came to inquire of the Lord, and they sat down before me.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, speak to these elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will not answer you a word, says the Lord.
Surely I will take vengeance with full vengeance. Son of man, testify to them about the lawless deeds of their fathers,

And say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: From the day that I took pleasure in the house of Israel, and appeared to the seed of the house of Jacob, and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt, and lifted up my hand to them with my own hand, and said: I am the Lord your God.

On that day I lifted up my hand to them with my own hand, to bring them out of the land of Egypt into the land that I had prepared for them, flowing with milk and honey; it is a honeycomb above every land.
And I said to them: Let each one of you put away the abominations of your eyes, and do not defile yourselves with the deeds of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

But they rebelled against me and would not listen to me. They did not put away the abominations of their eyes, and they did not abandon the deeds of Egypt. And I said that I would pour out my wrath upon them and carry out my anger among them in the land of Egypt.
And I acted so that my name would not be profaned at all before the nations among whom they are, and among whom I had appeared to them, in their sight, to bring them out of the land of Egypt.
And I brought them into the wilderness.
And I gave them my commandments and made my judgments known to them, which, if a person does them, he will live by them.
And I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, so that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

And I said to the house of Israel in the wilderness: Walk in my commandments. But they did not walk in them, and they cast away my judgments, which, if a person does them, he will live by them. And they greatly profaned my sabbaths. And I said that I would pour out wrath upon them in the wilderness to wipe them out.
And I acted so that my name would not be profaned at all before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.

And I lifted up my hand against them in the wilderness, swearing that I would by no means bring them into the land that I had given them, flowing with milk and honey; it is a honeycomb above every land,
because they cast away my judgments, and did not walk in my commandments, and kept profaning my sabbaths, and walked after the thoughts of their heart.
Yet my eye spared them, so that I did not wipe them out, and I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.
And I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not walk according to the law of your fathers, and do not keep their judgments, and do not take part in their ways.
I am the Lord your God. Walk in my commandments, keep my judgments, and do them.
And keep my sabbaths holy, and let them be a sign between me and you, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.

But their children also provoked me bitterly. They did not walk in my commandments, and they did not keep my judgments so as to do them, which, if a person does them, he would live by them. And they kept profaning my sabbaths. And I said that I would pour out my wrath and my anger upon them,
but I did not do it, so that my name would not be profaned at all among the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
And I lifted up my hand against them in the wilderness, swearing to scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the lands.
Because they did not keep my righteous laws, they turned away from my commandments, and they profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes followed the purposes of their fathers.
And I gave them commandments that were not good, and judgments by which they could not live.
And I defiled them through their own deeds, when I passed over everything that opens the womb, so that I might destroy them.

Therefore speak, son of man, to the rebellious house, the house of Israel, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Even until now your fathers have provoked me to anger by their sins, by which they sinned against me.

And I brought them into the land that I had lifted up my hand to give them, and they saw every high hill and every shady tree. And there they sacrificed to their idols, and there they set up a fragrant savor, and there they offered their sacrifices.
And I said to them: "What is Baal, that you go there?" And they called its name Baal, to this very day.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Are you defiling yourselves in the lawless deeds of your fathers, and going after their abominations?

And are you defiling yourselves with the firstfruits of your gifts and with your appointed offerings, to this very day? And shall I answer you a word, O house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not answer you, nor shall this come up into your heart.
And it shall not be as you say: "Let us be like all the nations and tribes of the earth, to serve wood and stones."
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, surely with a strong hand, and with a raised arm, and with fierce wrath I will reign over you.
And I will bring you out from the peoples, and I will gather you from the countries in which you were scattered among them, with a strong hand and with a raised arm and with fierce wrath.
And I will bring you into a wilderness, and there I will judge you face to face.
As I judged your fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, so I will judge you, says the Lord God.
And I will bring you under my rod, and I will bring you in by number.
And I will pick out from among you the ungodly and the rebels. And I will bring them out, and they shall not enter the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord God.

And you, O house of Israel, thus says the Lord God: Let each of you put away his deeds; and after that, if you listen to me, and if you do not profane my holy [?] name, I will no longer deal with you according to your gifts and according to your ways.

But on my holy mountain and on the high place, says the Lord God, there the whole house of Israel, all of it, shall serve me; and there I will accept them, and I will look upon your firstfruits and the firstfruits of your consecrated offerings.

As a sweet savor I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries in which you were scattered among them. And I will be holy among you before the eyes of the people.
And you shall know that I am the Lord God, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I stretched out my hand to give to your fathers.
And there you will remember your ways and your doings, by which you defiled yourselves. And you will strike your faces for all your wicked deeds.
And you will know that I am the Lord, when I deal with you in this way, so that my name may not be defiled according to your evil ways or according to your corrupt deeds, says Adonai the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Son of man, set your face firmly against Teman, and look toward Dagon, prophesying toward the forest, toward the ruler of Nageb.

And say to the ruler of Nageb: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it will devour every green tree in you and every dry tree. And the kindled flame will not be quenched, and every face will be burned in it, from the east to the north.
And all flesh will know that I am the Lord. I have kindled it, and it will not be quenched.
And I said: By no means, Lord! They are saying of me, 'Is this not just a parable he is telling?'
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Therefore prophesy, son of man. Set your face firmly toward Jerusalem, look toward their holy places, and prophesy toward the land of Israel,
and say: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw my dagger from its sheath, and I will destroy from you every liar and every lawless one.
Just as I will destroy them from you, so my dagger will be [?] from its sheath against all flesh, from the east to the north.
And all flesh will know that I am the Lord. I have drawn my dagger from its sheath, and it will not return again.
And you, son of man, groan with breaking loins, and groan bitterly before their eyes.

And if they say to you, 'Why are you groaning?', say to them: 'Because of the news, for it is coming.' And every heart will tremble, all hands will go slack, all flesh and every spirit will grow cold, and all thighs will be defiled with wetness. Behold, it is coming, and it will happen, says Adonai the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Sword, sword, be sharpened and be enraged,
so that you may slaughter the victims. Be sharpened so that you may gleam, made ready for destruction. Slay and treat with contempt, and strike every tree.
And he gave it, made ready to be held in his hand. The sword has been sharpened, and it is ready, made ready to be given into the hand of those who pierce.

Cry out and wail, son of man, for this has come upon my people. This has come upon all the leaders of Israel; they will dwell upon the sword. This has happened to my people. Therefore clap your hands,
for it has been justified. And what are you, rejected tribe? And that will not be, says Adonai the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy, clap hand against hand, and double the sword. The third sword is a sword of wounding; the sword of wounds is great. And make them startled,
so that the heart may tremble and the weakened may multiply. At all the gates they have been given over to slaughter by the sword. It has been made fit for slaughter; it has been made gleaming.
Pass through, be sharpened, devour on the right and on the left, wherever your face is turned.
And I will strike hand against hand, and I will let loose my anger upon them. I the Lord have spoken.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:

"And you, son of man, mark out for yourself two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to enter by. The two bands shall come out from one land. And you shall set a hand at the beginning of the way to the city, at the head of the way,
for the sword to enter into Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and into Idumea, and into Jerusalem in its midst.

For the king of Babylon shall stand at the first way, at the head of the two ways, to practise divination: to make the rod sprout [?], to inquire of the carved images, and to inspect the liver. At his right hand

shall be the divination against Jerusalem: to set an army against it, to open the mouth with shouting, to raise the voice with a war cry, to set an army against its gates, to heap up earth, and to build towers for archers.
And he himself will divine for them with divination before them, and he will bring their falsehood to remembrance, so that it is remembered.

Therefore thus says the Lord Lord: Because you have brought your falsehood to remembrance, so that your ungodliness was revealed, and your sins appear in all your ungodliness and in your deeds, because you have remembered, in these too you shall be seized.
And you, defiled and lawless ruler of Israel: has the day not now come, at the time of falsehood? An end.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: Take off the turban and put off the crown. This shall not be as it was. Bring low the high, and lift up the lowly.
And I have made it falsehood, and it shall not be as it was, until the one comes to whom it belongs, and I will give it to him.

And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord concerning the sons of Ammon and their reproach. And say to them: Sword, sword, drawn for slaughter and drawn for destruction, rise up so that you may gleam,
in your vain vision and in your lying divination, so that you are laid upon the necks of the wounded lawless ones, whose day comes at the time of falsehood. An end.
Return. Do not stay in the place where you were born. In your own land I will judge you.
And I will pour out my wrath upon you. With the fire of my anger I will blow upon you. And I will give you into the hands of the gentiles, doers of evil.
You shall be food for fire. Your blood shall be in the land. There shall be no remembrance of you, for I the Lord Lord have spoken."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
"And you, son of man, will you not judge this bloody city? Show it all its lawless deeds.
And say to it: Thus says Adonai the Lord: O bloody city, which has shed blood in your midst so that your time may come, and you made a design of your heart for yourself, to defile yourself

with the blood of those whom you shed, and you have fallen. And by the thoughts of your heart which you carried out among them you were defiled. And you have brought all your days near, and you have brought on the times of your years. Therefore I have given you up as a reproach to the gentiles and as a mockery to all lands,
to those near you and to those far from you. And they shall mock you, unclean one, notorious one, full of much lawlessness.
Behold, the rulers of the house of Israel, each one with his kin, were defiled in you so that they might shed blood.
In you they spoke evil of father and mother, and in you they dealt falsely with the stranger. In you they oppressed the widow and the orphan.
And they despised my holy things, and in you they profaned my sabbaths.
There were robbers in you who shed blood. In you they ate upon the mountains, and in you they committed impurity.
In you they uncovered their father's shame, and in you they humbled a woman in her impurity.
In you each man committed lawlessness with his neighbour's wife, and each one defiled his daughter-in-law lawlessly, and in you each man humbled his sister, his father's daughter.

In you they took bribes in order to shed blood. In you they took usury and interest. And I will bring to an end the full measure of your wickedness, done through oppression; but you have forgotten me, says Adonai the Lord.
If I strike my hand against you for what you have carried out, and for what you have done, and for the blood that has been shed in you —
will your heart stand firm against me, or will your hands hold out against me, in the days in which I will deal with you? I the Lord have spoken, and I will do it.
And I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the lands, and your impurities will be removed from you.
