And I will take possession of you before the eyes of the nations, and you will know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
Son of man, behold, the house of Israel has become mixed to me. All of them are like bronze and iron and lead and tin mixed in the midst of silver.
Therefore say to them: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because you have all become mixed together, therefore I will bring you into the midst of Jerusalem.
As bronze and iron and lead and tin and silver are put into the midst of a furnace to blow fire on them and to melt them, so I will bring you in with my wrath, and gather you, and melt you.
And I will blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted in the midst of it.
As silver is melted in the midst of furnaces, so you will be melted in the midst of it, and you will know that I am the Lord, and I will pour out my wrath upon you.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
Son of man, say to her: You are a land that has had no rain, and there was no dew on you on the day of wrath.
Her leaders in her midst were like roaring lions seizing prey. They devoured people's lives by force and took payment. Your widows multiplied in you.

Your priests despised my law and profaned my holy things. They did not distinguish between the holy and the profane, and they did not separate the chosen from the unchosen. They hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I was profaned among them.
And her rulers in her midst were like wolves seizing prey, shedding blood so that they might satisfy their greed.
And their prophets daubed them, and those seers of vain things fell, who divined falsehood and said, "Thus says the Lord," when the Lord had not spoken to them.
You wring the people of the land dry through falsehood, and you seize plunder. You oppress the afflicted and the poor, and you do not deal rightly with the stranger.
And I sought among them a man who would walk uprightly and stand before me for the land at all times, so that it might not be wiped out entirely, but I did not find one.
And I poured out my indignation upon them, to finish them off with the fire of my wrath; I have repaid their ways upon their own heads, says the Lord God.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother.
And they played the harlot in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts were pressed down, and there they lost their virginity.
And their names were Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister. They were mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Samaria is Oholah and Jerusalem is Oholibah.
And Oholah played the harlot before me and attached herself to her lovers, the Assyrians, her neighbours,
who were clothed in blue: leaders and governors, choice young men, all of them horsemen mounted on horses.
And she gave her harlotry to them, to all the choice sons of the Assyrians and to all on whom she doted, and with all her desire she defiled herself.
And she did not give up the harlotry she had practised in Egypt, for they lay with her in her youth, took away her virginity, and committed their harlotry with her.
Therefore I gave her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians, on whom she doted.
They exposed her shame, carried off her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and they took vengeance on her and on her daughters.
And her sister Oholibah saw this, and she was more corrupt in her lust than her sister, and her harlotry was greater than her sister's harlotry.
She turned to the sons of the Assyrians, rulers and governors, her neighbours, clothed in finery, horsemen mounted on horses, all of them choice young men.
And I saw that they were defiled; both of them went the same way.
And she added to her harlotry. She saw men carved on the wall, images drawn in paint,
wearing embroidered cloth around their waists and dyed turbans on their heads. All of them looked alike, like the sons of the Chaldeans of the land of their birth.
And she doted on them as soon as her eyes saw them, and she sent messengers to them in the land of the Chaldeans.
And the sons of Babylon came to her, to the bed of lodging, and defiled her with her harlotry. She was defiled among them, and her soul did not turn away from them.

And she displayed her harlotry and exposed her shame, and my soul turned away from her, just as her soul had turned away from them. And she displayed her harlotry and exposed her shame, and my soul turned away from her sister, just as my soul had turned away from David her father.
And you multiplied your harlotries, calling to mind the days of your youth, when you played the harlot in the land of Egypt.
And you gave yourself to the Chaldeans, whose bodies are like those of donkeys, and whose neighing is like the neighing of horses.
And you looked back on the lawlessness of your youth, which you committed in Egypt, in your dwelling place, where the breasts of your youth fell.
Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will raise up against you your lovers, from whom your soul has turned away, and I will bring them against you from every side.
The sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa, and all the sons of Assyria, and with them chosen young men, leaders and governors, and all the rulers and renowned men mounted on horses.

All of them will come against you from the north, with chariots and wheels and a single assembly; shields and bucklers [?], and they will set guards around you. And I will place judgment before them, and they will take vengeance on you by their judgments.

And I will set my jealousy against you, and they will deal with you in the wrath of my anger. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and they will cut down your survivors with the sword; they will carry off your sons and your daughters, and fire will consume what remains of you.
And they will strip you of your clothing and carry off the vessels you took pride in.
And I will turn your impiety away from you, and your fornication that came from the land of Egypt, and you will not lift your eyes to them, and you will no longer remember Egypt.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will give you into the hands of those who hate you, from whom your soul has turned away.

And they will deal with you in hatred, and they will carry off all that you laboured for and all that you toiled over, and you will be naked and shamed, and the shame of your fornication and of your ungodliness will be laid bare. Your fornication
has done this to you, because you fornicated after the nations and defiled yourself with their schemes.
And you walked in the way of your sister, so I will put her cup into your hand.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: You will drink your sister's cup, deep and wide, overflowing [?], until you are completely drunk.
And you will be filled with faintness, the cup of your sister Samaria, a cup of ruin.
You will drink it, and I will put an end to her feasts and new moons, for I the Lord have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
Because you forgot me and turned your back on me, you too will receive what is due for your ungodliness and your acts of fornication.
And the Lord said to me: Son of man, will you not judge Oholah and Oholibah and tell them of their lawlessness?
For they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their schemes, and they made the children they bore to me pass through the fire.
They even did this to me: they defiled my sanctuary and made my sabbaths an abomination.
When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they also entered my holy places to defile them. This is what they did inside my house.
And for the men coming from far away, to whom they sent messengers, as soon as they arrived you bathed, painted your eyes, and decked yourself with ornaments.
And you sat on a couch spread with coverings, with a table laid out in front of you, and they took delight in my incense and my oil.
And they made merry with mingled voices. And from the crowd of men, the men who had come from the wilderness, they put bracelets on their hands and a glorious crown on their heads.
And I said: Do they not commit adultery in these things? And she fornicated in the way of a harlot.
And they went in to her as men go in to a harlot. In the same way they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, to commit lawlessness.
And these righteous men will take vengeance on her with the vengeance due to an adulteress and the vengeance for blood, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Bring up a people against them, and give them over to terror and plunder.
And stone them with the stoning of the people, and pierce them with their swords. Their sons and their daughters they shall kill, and their houses they shall burn with fire.
And I will turn away ungodliness from the land, and all women shall be taught a lesson, and shall no longer act according to their ungodliness.
And your ungodliness shall be brought back upon you, and you shall bear the sins of your schemes, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, and said:
Son of man, write down for yourself this day, from this day on, since the king of Babylon pressed hard upon Jerusalem, from this very day.
And speak a parable to the house of those who embitter me, and say: Thus says the Lord Adonai: Set on a cauldron, and pour water into it.
And put pieces into it, every good piece, thigh and shoulder, stripped from the bone,
taken from choice sheep; and kindle the bones beneath them. It has boiled, it has seethed, and its bones have been cooked in its midst.
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: O bloody city, cauldron in which is its venom, and that venom has not gone out of it! Let them take it out piece by piece; no lot has fallen upon it.
For its blood is in its midst; I set it upon a solid rock. I did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with earth,
so that wrath might rise up to take vengeance. For vengeance I have put its blood upon the solid rock, so that it may not be covered.
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: I will make the firebrand great,
and I will pile up the wood, and kindle the fire, so that the flesh may melt and the broth boil away,
and it shall be set upon the coals, so that it may be heated and its bronze grow hot, and its uncleanness melt within it, and its venom be consumed.
And much venom shall not come out of it, and its venom shall be put to shame.
Because you were defiled, what if you are not cleansed again until I have filled up my wrath against you?

I the Lord have spoken; it shall come to pass, and I will do it. I will not pardon, nor will I have mercy; according to your ways and according to your schemes I will judge you, says Adonai the Lord. Therefore I will judge you according to your bloodshed, O unclean, notorious one, greatly embittering one.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said to me:
Son of man, behold, I am taking from you the desire of your eyes by a violent stroke; you shall not lament, nor weep.

Groan with the blood of your inward parts; be in mourning. Let your hair not be bound up upon you, nor your sandals on your feet; you shall not be comforted by their lips, and you shall eat the bread of men.
And I spoke to the people in the morning, as the Lord had commanded me in the evening, and so I did in the morning, as he had commanded me.
And the people said to me: Will you not tell us what this is that you are doing?
And I said to them: The word of the Lord came to me and said:

Say to the house of Israel: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the gathering of your strength and the desire of your eyes, and that which your souls spare; and your sons and your daughters, whom you have left behind, shall fall by the sword.
And you shall do so, just as I did: [?] as a likeness of their face [?]. You shall not be comforted, and you shall not eat the bread of men.

And your long hair shall be on your heads, and your shoes on your feet. You shall not mourn and you shall not weep, and you shall waste away in your falsehood, and each of you shall implore his brother.
And Ezekiel shall be a sign for you. According to all that I have done, so shall you do. When this comes, then you shall know that I am the Lord.

And you, son of man: will it not be on that day, the day when I take from them their strength, the height of their boasting, the desire of their eyes, the uplifting of their soul, their sons and their daughters,
that on that day the one who escapes will come to you to tell it in your ears?
On that day your mouth shall be opened to the one who escaped, and from then on you shall no longer be mute, and you shall be a sign to them. And they shall know that I am the Lord.
Against the sons of Ammon. And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
"Son of man, set your face firmly against the sons of Ammon, and prophesy against them.

And say to the sons of Ammon: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Because you gloated over my sanctuary when it was defiled, and over the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and over the house of Judah when they went into captivity,

therefore, behold, I will give you into the hands of the sons of Kedem as a possession, and they shall settle among you with all their camps, and they shall pitch their tents among you. They shall eat your fruit, and they shall drink your richness.
And I will give them the cities of the sons of Ammon as pasture for their camels, and the sons of Ammon as pasture for flocks, and you shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
For thus says Adonai the Lord: Because you clapped your hands, and stamped with your foot, and rejoiced in your heart over the land of Israel,

therefore I will stretch out my hand against you, and give you as plunder among the nations, and I will cut you off from the peoples, and destroy you with destruction from the lands, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
Against Moab. Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Because Moab and Seir said, 'Is not the house of Israel and of Judah just like all the nations?'
therefore, behold, I will break the shoulder of Moab from the cities on its heights, the choice land, the house of Beth-jeshimoth, above the spring of the city on the seaward side.
I will give it to the sons of Kedem, together with the sons of Ammon, as a possession, so that there shall be no possession of the sons of Ammon.
And on Moab too I will execute vengeance, and they shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
Against the Edomites. Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because Idumea took its vengeance, avenging itself on the house of Judah, and they remembered evil and took revenge,

therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: I will stretch out my hand against Idumea, and I will cut off from it man and beast, and I will make it a desolation, and those pursued from Teman shall fall by the sword.

And I will bring my vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of my people Israel, and they shall act against Idumea according to my wrath and my anger, and they shall know my vengeance, says the Lord, the Lord.
Against the Philistines. Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because the foreigners acted in vengeance, and with heartfelt gloating they stirred up vengeance, to blot out forever,
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: I will stretch out my hand against the foreigners, and I will destroy the judges, and I will wipe out the inhabitants of the seacoast.
And I will carry out great vengeance among them, and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I bring my vengeance upon them.
Concerning Tyre. And in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, because Tyre said about Jerusalem, 'Aha! She is broken; the nations have perished; she has turned to me; she that was full is laid waste,'
therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring up many peoples against you, as the sea rises up with its waves.
And they shall throw down your walls and destroy your towers, and I will scrape its soil away from it and make it a bare rock.
It shall be a place for drying nets in the midst of the sea, for I the Lord have spoken, says Adonai the Lord; and it shall become plunder for the nations.
And her daughters in the field shall fall by the sword, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

For thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will send against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north; he is a king of kings, with horses and chariots and horsemen and a very great host of many nations.

He shall kill with the sword your daughters who are in the field, and he shall set guards [?] against you, and build a wall around you, and bring an army against you, and set armed men against you, and set his spears before you.
Your walls and your towers they shall throw down with his sword.

Because of the multitude of his horses his dust shall cover you, and at the noise of his horses and the wheels of his chariots your walls shall shake when he enters your gates, as one enters a city from the plain.
Your streets shall be trampled by the gear of his horses; he shall kill your people with the sword, and he shall throw the strength of your might to the ground.

And he shall carry off your power and plunder all your produce, and throw down your wall, and destroy your pleasant houses, and he shall throw your stones, your timber and your soil into the midst of the sea.
And he shall silence the multitude of your musicians, and the voice of your singers shall be heard no more.
And I will make you a hard rock; you shall be a place for drying nets, and you shall not be rebuilt, for I the Lord have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord, to Tyre: At the sound of your fall, at your groaning over the wounds, at the killing by the sword in your midst, the islands shall shake.

And all the rulers of the nations of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and take the crowns from their heads, and strip off their many-coloured ornaments. They shall be utterly terrified and sit on the ground, and they shall be afraid because of your destruction and groan over you.
And they shall raise a lament over you and say to you: How you have been destroyed from the sea, you renowned city, who spread fear of you among the inhabitants around you!
And the islands were afraid from the day of your fall.
For thus says Adonai the Lord: When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are not inhabited, when you bring up the deep against you, and many waters cover you.

And I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of eternity. I will make you dwell in the depth of the earth like an everlasting desolation, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited and will not rise again to life.
I will hand you over to destruction, and you will be no more, forever, says Adonai the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Son of man, take up a lament over Tyre, and say to Tyre, which dwells at the entrance of the sea, the trading-place of the nations from many islands:
Thus says Adonai the Lord to Tyre: You said, “I have clothed myself, by myself, in my beauty.”
In the heart of the sea, for the Geelim [?], your sons adorned you with beauty.
You were built of fir from Senir. [?] of cypress boards were brought to you from Lebanon to make ship-[?] (masts?).
They made your oars from Bashan. They made your temples of ivory, and wooded [?] houses from the islands of Kittim.
They made embroidered fine linen from Egypt into a bed for you, to clothe you in glory. Blue and purple from the islands of Elishah were for your adornment, and they became your garment.
And of your rulers, those who lived in Sidon and the Aradians were your helmsmen. Your wise men, O Tyre, who were in you, were your sailors.
The elders of Babylon and their wise men who were in you strengthened your counsel. All the ships of the sea and their [?] oarsmen were yours, from the west, from the farthest west [text garbled].
Persians and Lydians and Libyans were in your army. Men of war hung shields and helmets in you. They gave you your glory.
The sons of the Aradians and your army were on your walls and were the guards of your towers. They hung their quivers all around your mountains. They made your beauty perfect.
The Carthaginians were your merchants because of the abundance of all your strength. They brought silver and gold and iron and copper and lead and tin to your quarters.
Hellas and all the land and the regions around it traded with you in human souls. They brought vessels of bronze to your market.
From the house of Togarmah they brought horses and horsemen to your market.
The sons of the Rhodians, merchants from the islands, increased your trade with ivory [?] (tusks?). And you gave your payment to those who brought them in.
Men traded with you because of the great number of your foreigners. They brought stacte, many-coloured dyed goods from Tarshish, and Ramoth and Chorchor to your market.
The sons of Judah and Israel were your merchants in the sale [?] of wheat. They brought ointment and cassia and choice honey and oil and resin to your markets.
Damascus was your merchant because of the abundance of your power. They brought wine from Helbon, wool from Miletus, and wine to your markets.
Wrought iron from Asael and chariot wheels are among your foreigners.
Dedan was your merchant in choice horses for chariots.
Arabia and the princes of Kedar were merchants under your hand, in camels and rams and lambs, in which they traded with you.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah were your merchants in choice spices. They brought fine carbuncle and gold to your market.
Haran and Canneh were your merchants. Asshur and Charman were your merchants.
They brought merchandise of hyacinth (blue stuff), and choice treasures bound with cords, and of cypress, in ships.
The Carthaginians were your merchants; you were filled with the multitude of your foreign traders, and you became very heavy in the heart of the sea.
Your rowers brought you into many waters; the south wind crushed you in the heart of the sea.

Your strength and your wages and those of your foreign traders, and your rowers, and your toiling ship-masters, your counselors and your foreign traders, and your sailors from among your foreign traders, and all your fighting men in you, and all your company in your midst fell in the heart of the sea on the day of your fall.
At the sound of your cry your toiling sailors were afraid;
and all the rowers and those who sat in them came down from their ships, and all the rowers of the ships of the sea, and they stood on the land.
They will cry out over you with a loud voice, and wail bitterly, and pour earth on their heads, and strew ashes on themselves.
And their sons will take up a lament, a lament for Tyre:
How much, or what wages did you find from the sea? You filled the nations from your abundance, and from your foreign traders you enriched all the kings of the earth.
And now you are shattered in the sea; in the depth of the water are your foreign traders and all your company, and all who were in your midst fell, and all your rowers.
The inhabitants of the islands were distressed over you, and their kings were struck with terror; they were astonished, and their faces were in tears.
The merchants from among the nations hissed at you; you have become a destruction, and you shall be no more forever.
Concerning the king of Tyre. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

And you, son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because your heart was lifted up, and you said, 'I am a god; I have inhabited the dwelling of God in the heart of the sea'—yet you are a man and not God, and you made your heart like the heart of God.
Are you then wiser than Daniel? Did the wise not teach you their knowledge?
Was it by your knowledge or by your wisdom that you made power for yourself, and silver and gold in your treasuries?
Or by your great knowledge and your understanding did you increase your power?
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Because you set your heart like the heart of God,

in return for this, behold, I will send against you foreigners, the foul ones from among the nations, and they will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your knowledge, and they will bring that beauty of yours to destruction.
And they will bring you down, and you will die the death of the wounded in the heart of the sea.
Will you indeed speak and say, 'I am a god,' before those who kill you? But you are a man and not God.
Among the multitude of the uncircumcised you will die by the hand of foreigners, for I have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, take up a lament over the prince of Tyre, and say to him: Thus says Adonai the Lord: You are a seal of [?], a likeness, and a crown of beauty.

You were in the delight of the paradise of God. Every precious stone covered you: sardius and topaz, and emerald, carbuncle and sapphire, and jasper, and silver and gold, and ligure and agate, and amethyst and chrysolite, and beryl and onyx. And you filled your treasuries and your storehouses within you with gold.
From the day you were created, together with the cherub, I set you on my holy mountain; you were in the midst of the stones of fire.
You walked blameless in your days, from the day you were created until the day when falsehood was found in you.
From the abundance of your trade you filled your treasuries with lawlessness, and you sinned and were wounded; and the cherub brought you down from the mountain of God, from among the stones of fire.

Your heart was exalted because of your beauty; your knowledge was corrupted along with your beauty, because of the multitude of your sins. I cast you down to the earth; I gave you up before kings to be made a mockery.

By the multitude of your sins and by the falsehood of your trade your sanctuaries were defiled, and I will bring forth fire from your midst; it will devour you, and I will turn you to ashes on your land before all who see you.
And all among the nations who knew you will be grieved over you. You have become a ruin, and you will be no more forever.
Concerning Sidon. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face against Sidon, and prophesy against it,
and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you, and you will know that I am the Lord, when I execute judgment in you and am sanctified in you.
Blood and death will be in your streets, and the wounded will fall by the sword in you and all around you, and they will know that I am the Lord.
And there will no longer be for the house of Israel a goad of bitterness and a thorn of pain from those around them who despise them, and they will know that I am the Lord.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will gather Israel from the nations where they were scattered, and I will be sanctified among them before the peoples and the nations, and they will dwell in their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

And they will dwell on it in security, and build houses, and plant vineyards, and dwell in them in security, when I execute judgment on all who despise them, all who are around them; and they will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.
In the tenth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against you, you great sea-monster, who lies in the midst of his rivers, who says, 'The rivers are mine, and I made them.'
And I will put a hook in your jaws, and I will make the fish of your rivers stick to your fins, and I will bring you up out of the midst of your river, together with all the fish of your river.

And I will cast you down quickly, you and all the fish of your river; you will fall on the face of the open field, and you will not be gathered up, nor will anyone wrap you for burial. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky.
And all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord, because you have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
When they took hold of you by the hand, you were crushed; and when every hand struck upon them, and when they leaned upon you, you broke and crushed all their strength.
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy people from you and livestock from the land.
And the land of Egypt shall be destroyed and desolate, and they shall know that I am the Lord, because you said, 'The rivers are mine, and I made them.'
Therefore, behold, I am against you and against your rivers, and I will give the land of Egypt over to desolation and destruction, from Migdol and Syene as far as the border of Ethiopia.
No human foot shall pass through it, and no foot of livestock shall tread it, and it shall not be inhabited for forty years.

And I will give its land over to destruction in the midst of desolated lands, and its cities shall be in the midst of desolated cities for forty years; and I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the countries.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they had been scattered.
And I will bring back the captivity of Egypt, and I will settle them in the land of Pathros, the land from which they had been carried off, and it shall be a small kingdom.
It shall be the least of all kingdoms, and it shall no longer exalt itself over the nations, and I will make them few, so that they may not be many among the nations.
And they shall no longer be a hope for the house of Israel, bringing iniquity to remembrance, so that they may not follow after them; and they shall know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And it came to pass in the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, that the word of the Lord came to me and said:

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made his army labor with great labor against Tyre; every head [?], and every shoulder was bowed down; yet no wages were given to him or to his people for Tyre, nor for the labor with which he labored against it.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I give to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, the land of Egypt, and he shall carry off its captives and seize its spoil, and it shall be the wages for his army.
In return for the service with which he labored against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt. Thus says Adonai the Lord.
On that day a horn shall spring up for all the house of Israel, and I will give you an opened mouth in their midst, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said:
You, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Alas, alas for the day!
For the day of the Lord is near; the end of the nations is coming.
And a sword shall come upon the Egyptians, and there shall be trembling in Ethiopia, and the wounded shall fall in Egypt, and its dwellings shall be destroyed.
Persians and Cretans and Lydians and Libyans, and all the sojourners, the sons of my covenant, shall fall by the sword with them in it.
And the strength of Egypt shall fall, and the insolence [?] of its might shall be brought low; from Migdol as far as Syene they shall fall by the sword in it, says the Lord, the Lord.
And they shall be desolated in the midst of desolated countries, and their cities shall be in the midst of desolated cities.
And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are crushed.
On that day angels shall go out in haste to destroy Ethiopia, and there shall be turmoil among them on that day of Egypt, for behold, it is coming.
Thus says the Lord: I will destroy the multitude of the Egyptians by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
By his hand and the hand of his people, the defiled ones of the nations, sent to destroy the land. They shall all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land shall be filled with the wounded.
And I will make their rivers desolate. I will destroy the land and everything in it by the hand of foreigners, for I, the Lord, have spoken.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: I will destroy the great ones of Memphis, and there shall be no more princes in the land of Egypt.
And I will destroy the land of Pathros, and set fire to Tanis, and take vengeance on Diospolis.
And I will pour out my wrath on Sais, the strength of Egypt, and I will destroy the multitude of the Memphites.
And I will set fire to Egypt, and Syene shall tremble greatly, and Diospolis shall be breached, and the waters shall be scattered.
The young men of Heliopolis (the City of the Sun) and of Bubastis shall fall by the sword, and their wives shall go into captivity.
And at Tahpanhes the day shall grow dark when I break the tribe of Egypt, and I will destroy the insolence of her strength. A cloud shall cover her, and their daughters shall be led away captive.
And I will execute judgment on Egypt, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, I have broken the arms of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and they have not been bound up to heal him, to put a salve on him, or to give him strength to hold the sword.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt. I will break his strong and outstretched arms, and I will make his sword fall from his hand.
And I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands.
And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hands. He shall bring that sword against Egypt, carry off her spoil, and take her plunder.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and the arms of Pharaoh shall fall. And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I put my sword into the hands of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out over the land of Egypt.
And I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his multitude: To whom have you likened yourself in your loftiness?
Behold, Assyria was like a cypress of Lebanon, with fine branches and of great height, and its top was among the clouds.
The water made it grow, and the deep raised it up. It brought its rivers around its plantings and sent out its dense branches to all the trees of the field.
Therefore it grew taller than all the trees of the field, and its branches spread out because of the many waters.
All the birds of the sky nested on its shoots, and all the wild beasts of the field gave birth under its boughs; all the multitudes of the nations dwelt in its shade.
And it was beautiful in its height and in the abundance of its boughs, for its roots were by many waters.

And the cedars in the paradise of God were not like it, and the pines were not like its shoots, and the palm trees were not like its boughs, and no tree in the paradise of God was like it in its beauty.
And because of the abundance of its boughs, the trees of the paradise of delight of God envied it.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you became great in your greatness, and your tops reached up among the clouds, and I saw it in its exaltation,
I gave it into the hands of the ruler of the nations, and he brought about its destruction.

And strangers, foul men from among the nations, cut it down and threw it down upon the mountains. Its boughs fell in all the valleys, and its wood was broken in every plain of the earth. All the peoples of the nations came down from its shelter and trampled it.
At its fall all the birds of the sky rested on it, and all the beasts of the field were under that tree.

This was so that none of the trees by the waters would be exalted in their greatness, or raise their tops up among the clouds, or stand in their height. And all who drank water with them were all given over to death, to the depths of the earth, among the sons of men who go down to the pit.

Thus says the Lord: On the day it went down to hell, the abyss mourned for it. He set its rivers against it, and I held back many waters. Lebanon grew dark over it, and all the trees of the field fainted over it.

The nations were shaken at the sound of its fall, when they brought it down to hell with those who go down to the pit. And under the earth all the trees of delight and the choice trees of Lebanon, all that drink water, comforted it.
For they too went down to hell with it, among those wounded by the sword. And its offspring, who dwelt under its shelter, perished in the midst of their life.

Whom have you come to resemble? You were cast down [?] and went down with the trees of delight to the depths of the earth. You will sleep among the uncircumcised, with those wounded by the sword. So shall it be with Pharaoh and all the multitude of his might, says the Lord, the Lord.
And in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and say to him: You were like a lion of the nations, and like the dragon in the sea you butted with your horns in your rivers. You stirred up the waters with your foot and trampled your rivers.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: A net of many peoples has surrounded you, and I will bring you up with my hook.
And I will spread you out on the land, and the plains will be filled with you. I will set all the birds of the sky upon you, and I will fill all the beasts of the whole earth with you.
And I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill them with your blood.
And the land will be watered with what flows out of you, from your great mass on the mountains; I will fill the ravines with you.
And I will cover you when the heaven is extinguished over you, and its stars grow dark. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not show its light.
All that shine in the heavens will grow dark over you, and I will put darkness on your land, says the Lord, the Lord.
And I will provoke the hearts of many peoples to anger when I bring your captives among the nations, into a land that you did not know.
And many nations will be distressed over you, and their kings will be utterly terrified when my sword flies before their faces. From the day of your fall they will wait for their own fall.
For thus says Adonai the Lord: The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you.
With the swords of mighty men I will cast down your strength, all the defiled ones from among the nations. They will destroy the insolence of Egypt, and all its strength will be shattered.
I will destroy all its livestock from beside many waters. The foot of man will no longer stir the waters up, and the tracks of livestock will not trample them.
So then their waters will become still, and their rivers will flow like oil, says Adonai the Lord.
When I hand Egypt over to destruction, and the land is laid waste with all that fills it, when I scatter all its inhabitants, then they will know that I am the Lord.
It is a lament, and you shall lament over it. The daughters of the nations will lament over Egypt, and they will lament over all its strength, says the Lord, the Lord.
And in the twelfth year, in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, lament over the strength of Egypt. Their daughters of the nations will bring them down dead into the depth of the earth, with those who go down to the pit.
They will fall with him among those slain by the sword, and all his strength will sleep.
And the mighty men will say to you: Go down into the depth of the pit. Whom are you better than? Go down [?] and sleep with the uncircumcised among those slain by the sword.
Assyria is there with all his assembly, and all those slain by the sword were laid there,
and their grave is in the depth of the earth. His assembly was around his grave, and all his slain had fallen by the sword, those who had spread terror of themselves in the land of the living.

Elam is there with all his host around his grave. All are slain, fallen by the sword, those who went down uncircumcised into the depth of the earth, who had spread terror of themselves in the land of the living. They bore their torment with those who go down to the pit.
among those slain by the sword,
Meshech and all their host were laid there. All their slain are around their grave, all uncircumcised, slain by the sword, those who had spread terror of themselves in the land of the living.

And they slept with the mighty men who fell by the sword long ago, who went down to hell with their weapons of war. They laid their swords under their heads, and their iniquities lay on their bones, because they had terrified the mighty men during their lives.
And you will sleep with the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.
The princes of Assyria were laid there, who gave up his strength to be slain by the sword. They slept, slain, with those who go down to the pit.

There are the princes of the north, all the leaders of the people of Assyria, who went down wounded. With their terror and their might they have fallen asleep among the uncircumcised, wounded by the sword, and they have borne their torment with those who go down to the pit.
Pharaoh saw them and was comforted for all his host, says Adonai the Lord.

For I have put their terror in the land of the living, and they shall sleep among the uncircumcised, with those wounded by the sword. So it shall be with Pharaoh and all his multitude, says Adonai the Lord.
To the sons of Jacob. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, speak to the sons of your people and say to them: Suppose I bring a sword upon a land, and the people of that land take one man from among them and set him up as their watchman.
He sees the sword coming upon the land, blows the trumpet and warns the people.
Then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not take heed, and the sword comes and overtakes him, his blood shall be on his own head.
For he heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take heed; his blood shall be upon him. But the one who took heed has saved his soul.

But suppose the watchman sees the sword coming and does not give warning with the trumpet, and the people do not take heed, and the sword comes and takes a soul from among them. That person was given over because of his own lawlessness, but I will require his blood from the hand of the watchman.
And you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel, and you shall hear words from my mouth.

When I say to the sinner, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not tell that lawless man so that he might turn from his lawlessness, that lawless man shall die in his lawlessness, but I will require his blood from your hands.

But if you warn the ungodly man about his way beforehand, so that he might turn from it, and he does not turn from his evil way, that lawless man shall die in his own lawlessness, but you will have saved your soul.
And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: This is what you say: 'Our stumblings and our lawless deeds are upon us, and we are wasting away in them. How then shall we live?'

Say to them: As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the ungodly, but that the ungodly turn from his way and live. Turn, turn back from your way! Why will you perish, O house of Israel?

Say to the sons of your people: The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him on the day he goes astray. The lawlessness of the ungodly shall do him no harm on the day he turns from his lawlessness. And the righteous shall not be saved on the day of his sin.

If I say to the righteous man, 'You shall surely live,' and he trusts in his own righteousness and commits lawlessness, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered. He shall die in the sin that he committed.
And if I say to the lawless man, 'You shall surely die,' and he turns from his sin and does justice and righteousness,
gives back the debtor's pledge, repays what he has robbed, and walks in the commandments of life so as to commit sin no more, he shall surely live and shall not die.
None of the sins that he committed shall be remembered, because he has done what is just and right; he shall live in these,
And the sons of your people will say: "The way of the Lord is not right"; but it is that way of theirs that is not right.
If a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits lawlessness, he shall die in it.
And if the sinner turns back from his lawlessness and does judgment and righteousness, he shall live by them.
And this is what you say: "The way of the Lord is not right." I will judge you, each one according to your ways, O house of Israel.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month of our captivity, that one who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said: "The city has been taken by the enemies."
And the hand of the Lord was upon me in the evening, until he came; and my mouth was opened when he came to me in the morning. And once my mouth was opened, it was no longer held shut.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
"Son of man, those who live in that desolate land of Israel are saying: 'Abraham was one man, and he possessed the land; but we are many, and the land has been given to us to possess.'
Therefore say to them:

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: As I live, surely those in the desolate places shall fall by the sword, and those who are in the open field shall be given to the wild beasts for food, and those who were in the walled cities and in the caves I will destroy by death.
And I will make that land a desolation, and the insolence of its strength shall perish, and the mountains of Israel shall be laid waste, for there shall be no one passing through it.
And they shall know that I am the Lord. And I will make their land a desolation, and it shall be laid waste because of all their abominations that they have committed.

And you, son of man: the sons of your people talk about you by the walls and at the doors of their houses; and a man speaks to his brother and says to him: 'Let us gather and hear the words that come out of the mouth of the Lord.'

And they will come to you as a people gathers, and they will sit before you and listen to your words, but they will not do them; for falsehood is in their mouth, and their hearts follow after filthiness.
And you are to them like the sound of a harp, a sweet-sounding and well-tuned voice; and they will listen to your words, but they will not do them.
And when it comes, they will say: 'Behold, it has come'; and they will know that a prophet has been among them."
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and say to those shepherds: Thus says Adonai the Lord: O you shepherds of Israel! Do the shepherds not feed themselves? Do the shepherds not feed the sheep?
Behold, you eat the milk, and clothe yourselves with the wool, and slaughter the fat ones, but you did not feed my sheep.

You did not strengthen the weak, and you did not fatten the sick, and you did not bind up the broken, you did not bring back the one that strayed, and you did not seek the lost; and the strong you treated with hard labor.
And my sheep were scattered, because there was no shepherd; and they became food for all the beasts of the field.

And my sheep were scattered over all the mountains and over all the high hills, and they were scattered over the face of all the earth; they were scattered, and there was no one to seek them or to bring them back.
Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

As I live, says Adonai the Lord: because my sheep have become prey and food for all the beasts of the field, because there were no shepherds, and the shepherds did not seek out my sheep, and the shepherds fed themselves and did not feed my sheep,
therefore, O shepherds,

thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against the shepherds. I will seek out my sheep and take them from your hand, and I will turn the shepherds away, so that they no longer tend my sheep, and those shepherds shall no longer feed them. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, and they shall no longer be food for them.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will seek out my sheep and look after them,

as a shepherd seeks his flock on a day of cloud and mist, when his sheep are scattered far apart. So I will seek out my sheep, and I will bring them back from all the places where they were scattered on that day of cloud and mist.

I will bring them out from among the nations and gather them from the countries, and I will bring them into their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in every inhabited place of the land.

I will feed them in good pasture on the high mountains of Israel, and their folds shall be there. There they shall lie down, and there they shall rest in good delight, and they shall graze on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I will feed my sheep, and I will give them rest, and they shall know that I am the Lord. Thus says Adonai the Lord:
I will seek out the lost and bring back the strayed. I will bind up the broken and strengthen the weak. I will guard the strong, and I will feed them with justice.
And as for you, my sheep, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will judge between sheep and sheep, and between ram and he-goat.
Is it not enough for you that you grazed on the good pasture? You trampled the rest of the pasture with your feet. You drank the clear water, and you muddied the rest with your feet.
And my sheep grazed on what you had trampled, and drank the water that your feet had churned up.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will judge between the strong sheep and the weak sheep.
For you shoved with your flanks and your shoulders, you butted with your horns, and you oppressed every weak one.
I will save my sheep, and they shall no longer be prey, and I will judge between ram and ram.
I will raise up a shepherd over them, and my servant David shall tend them, and he shall be their shepherd.
And I the Lord will be their God, and David a ruler among them. I the Lord have spoken.
I will make a covenant of peace with David. I will remove the evil beasts from the land, and they shall dwell in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
I will give them the places round about my mountain, and I will give you rain, a rain of blessing.

The trees of the field shall yield their fruit, and the earth shall yield its strength. They shall dwell in their land in the hope of peace, and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I break their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
And they shall no longer be plunder for the nations, and the beasts of the earth shall no longer devour them. They shall live in hope, and there shall be no one to frighten them.
And I will raise up for them a plant of peace, and they shall no longer perish from famine on the earth, and they shall no longer suffer reproach from the nations.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, and that they are my people, the house of Israel, said Adonai the Lord.
You are my sheep, the sheep of my flock, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord Lord.
Concerning the Edomites. And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir, and prophesy against it.
And say to it: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolation, and you shall be laid waste.
And I will lay waste your cities, and you shall be desolate, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
Because you became an everlasting enemy, and with treachery you lay in wait against the house of Israel, by the hand of enemies, with the sword, in the time of falsehood, at the end.
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord Lord, you have surely sinned to the point of blood, and blood shall pursue you.
And I will make Mount Seir a desolate wilderness, and I will destroy from it both people and livestock.
And I will fill your hills and your valleys with your slain, and in all your plains those slain by the sword shall fall in your midst.
And I will make you a desolation forever, and your cities shall no longer be inhabited, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
Because you said, 'The two nations and the two lands shall be mine, and I will take possession of them' — yet the Lord is there.
Therefore, as I live, says Adonai the Lord, I will deal with you according to your enmity, and I will make myself known among you when I judge you.
And you shall know that I am the Lord. I have heard the sound of your blasphemies, for you said: 'The mountains of Israel are desolate; they have been given to us for food.'
And with your mouth you spoke great boasts against me, and I have heard them.
Thus says the Lord: To the joy of all the earth I will make you desolate.
You shall be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Idumea shall be wiped out, and you shall know that I am the Lord their God.
Concerning the Idumeans. And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say to the mountains of Israel: Hear the word of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord Lord: Because the enemy said against you, 'Aha! The everlasting desolation has become our inheritance,'

therefore prophesy and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because you were despised and hated by those around you, so that you would become a possession for the remnant of the nations, and you became a byword among the tongues and a reproach among the nations, therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate and ruined places, and to the abandoned cities, which have been plundered and trampled by all the remnant of the nations around them.

Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Surely in the fire of my wrath I have spoken against the remnant of the nations and against all Idumea, because they seized my land as their own inheritance with [?] (literally 'with appeasement/rest'), and they treated souls with contempt, to ruin them by plunder.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my wrath because of the reproach of the nations, which you have borne.
Therefore I will lift up my hand against the nations that are around you, and they will receive their own disgrace.
But you, mountains of Israel, my people will eat your grapes and your fruit, for they are close to coming.
For behold, I am for you, for I will look upon you, and you will be worked.
And I will multiply people on you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruined places will be rebuilt.
And I will multiply people and livestock on you. I will settle you as you were at first and do good to you as before, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And I will bring forth people upon you, my people Israel, and they will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will no longer be left childless by them.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: Because they said to you, 'You are a devourer of people, and you have become bereaved of your offspring,'
therefore you will no longer devour people, and you will no longer leave your peoples childless, says the Lord, the Lord.
The disgrace of the nations will no longer be heard against you, and you will no longer bear the reproach of the peoples, says Adonai the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, the house of Israel lived in their land, and they defiled it with their way, with their idols, and with their uncleanness. Their way before me became like the uncleanness of a woman set apart in her impurity.
And I sent my wrath upon them,
and I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them among the countries. I judged them according to their way and according to their sin.
And they went among the nations, wherever they went, and they profaned my holy name, because they were called 'this people of the Lord,' and they had gone out of their land.
And I spared them for the sake of my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations wherever they went.

Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says Adonai the Lord: It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you profaned among the nations wherever you went.
And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the nations, and the nations will know that I am the Lord, when I am sanctified among you before their eyes.
And I will bring you out from the nations, gather you from every land, and bring you into your own land.
And I will sprinkle holy water on you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleanness and from all your idols, and I will cleanse you.
And I will give you a new heart, and I will give you a new spirit. I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
And I will put my spirit upon you, and I will cause you to walk in my commandments and to keep my judgments and do them.
And you will live in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you will be my people, and I will be your God.
And I will save you from all your uncleannesses, and I will call for the grain and multiply it, and I will not bring famine upon you.
And I will multiply the fruit of the trees and the produce of the fields, so that you will never again bear the reproach of famine among the nations.
And you will remember your evil ways and your doings that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves before their face because of your iniquities.
It is not for your sake that I do this, says the Lord Adonai. Let it be known to you: be ashamed and be confounded because of your ways, O house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord Adonai: On the day when I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the desolate places will be rebuilt.
And the ruined land will be tilled, because it had lain ruined before the eyes of everyone who passed by. And they will say:
"That ruined land has become like a garden of delight, and the cities that were desolate, ruined and torn down have been resettled, fortified and strong."
And the nations, as many as are left around you, will know that I am the Lord, who rebuilt what was torn down and replanted what was ruined. I the Lord have spoken, and I have done it.
Thus says the Lord Adonai: For this too I will let the house of Israel seek me, so that I may do it for them: I will multiply the men among them like sheep,
like holy sheep, like the sheep of Jerusalem at her feasts. So shall those desolate cities be, full of flocks of men, and they will know that I am the Lord.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the Lord and set me down in the middle of a plain, and it was full of human bones.
And he led me around among them on every side, and behold, there were very many of them on the face of the plain, and they were very dry.
And the Lord said to me: "Son of man, will these bones live?" And I said: "Lord, you know that."
And the Lord said to me: "Prophesy over these bones and say to them: You dry bones, hear the word of the Lord."
Thus says the Lord Lord to these dry bones: Behold, I will bring the spirit of life upon you.
And I will put sinews on you, and make flesh grow over you, and stretch skin over you; and I will put my spirit into you, and you will live, and you will know that I am the Lord.
And I prophesied as the Lord had commanded me. And as I prophesied, behold, there was a shaking, and the bones came together, each to its own joint.
And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh was growing, and skin was covering them over, but there was still no spirit in them.
And the Lord said to me: "Son of man, prophesy and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord Adonai: Come from the four winds of heaven, O spirit, and breathe into these dead, and let them live."
And I prophesied as the Lord had commanded me, and the spirit entered them, and they lived and stood up on their feet, a very great multitude.
And the Lord spoke to me and said: "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. And they say: Our bones have dried up; our hope has perished; we are destroyed."
"Therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will open your graves, and bring you up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel."
And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves and bring my people up out of the graves.
And I will put my spirit upon you, and you shall live, and I will settle you in your land, and you shall know that I am the Lord; I have spoken and I will do it, says the Lord, the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:

Son of man, take for yourself a rod, and write upon it Judah and the sons of Israel who are on his side; and take a second rod, and write upon it Joseph, the rod of Ephraim, and all the sons of Israel who had turned to him.
And join them to one another into one rod, binding them together, and they shall be in your hand.
And it shall be, when the sons of Israel say to you: Will you not tell us what this means to you?

Then say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring the tribe of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him, and I will give them to the tribe of Judah, and they shall be one rod in the hand of Judah.
And the rods on which you write shall be in your hand before them.

And say to them: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I will bring the whole house of Israel out from among the nations into which they went, and I will gather them from all around them, and I will bring them into the land of Israel.

And I will make them one nation in my land and on the mountains of Israel; and one prince shall be over them, and they shall no longer be two nations, nor shall they be divided any more into two kingdoms.

So that they shall no longer defile themselves with their idols, and I will deliver them from all their iniquities in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them, and they shall be my people, and I the Lord will be their God.
And my servant David shall be prince among them, and there shall be one shepherd of them all, for they shall walk in my commandments and keep my judgments and do them.
And they shall dwell in their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell upon it, and David my servant shall be their prince forever.
And I will make with them a covenant of peace; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them, and I will establish my sanctuary among them forever.
And my dwelling shall be among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And the nations shall know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them, when my sanctuary is among them forever.
Concerning Gog. And the word of the Lord came to me, and said:
Son of man, set your face against Gog, the land of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal; and prophesy against him.
And say to him: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal,
And I will gather you and all your host, horses and horsemen, all of them armed with mail, a great multitude with shields and helmets and swords;
Persians and Ethiopians and Libyans, all of them with shields [?] and helmets;
Gomer and all those around him, the house of Togarmah from the farthest parts of the north, and all those around him, and many peoples with you.
Prepare, and make yourself ready, you and all your company that is gathered with you, and be kept in reserve for me beforehand.

After many days you will be made ready, and in your last years you will come and arrive at the land that has been brought back from the sword, made up of people gathered from many nations, to the land of Israel, which had become wholly desolate. And this people came out from among the nations, and they all dwelt in peace.
And you will come up like rain, and arrive like a cloud to cover the land, you and all who are with you, and many nations with you.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: And it will be on that day that thoughts will come up into your heart, and you will devise an evil plan.

And you will say: I will go up to that abandoned land, and I will come upon those who live in quiet and those who dwell in peace, all the inhabitants of the land, where there are no walls, no bars, and no gates.

I will carry off plunder and take their captives captive, to turn my hand against the desolated land that has been resettled, and against the nations gathered from many peoples, who have acquired possessions and who dwell at the navel of the earth.

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Carthage and all their villages will say to you: Have you come to plunder? Have you gathered your assembly to take spoil, to carry off silver and gold, to carry off possessions, and to take spoil?
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: Thus says Adonai the Lord: Is it not on that day, when my people Israel dwell in peace, that you will rise up?
And you will come from your place, from the far end of the north, and many nations with you, all riding up on horses, a great assembly and a numerous people.

And you will come up against my people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. It will be in the last days, and I will bring you up against my land, so that all the nations may know me, when I am glorified through you before them.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord, to Gog: You are the one of whom I spoke in the former days by the hand of my servants the prophets of Israel, in those days and years, about bringing you up against them.
And it will be on that day, the day when Gog comes to the land of Israel, says Adonai the Lord, that my wrath will rise up,
and my jealousy with the fire of my anger. And I have said that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

And at the presence of the Lord the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the wild beasts of the field, all the creeping things that crawl on the earth, and all people on the face of the earth will shake. The mountains will be torn apart, the ravines will collapse, and every wall in the land will fall to the ground.
And I will call down on him every terror of the sword, says the Lord. Every man's sword will be turned against his brother.
And I will judge him with death and blood, with torrential rain and hailstones, and I will rain fire and brimstone on him, on all who are with him, and on many nations.
And I will show my greatness and be glorified, and I will show my holiness and reveal myself before many nations, and they will know that I am the Lord, the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says Adonai the Lord: See, I am against you, Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal.
I will gather you and lead you, and I will bring you up from the far end of the north and bring you to the mountains of Israel.
And I will destroy your bow from your left hand, and your arrows from your right hand.

And I will cast you down upon the mountains of Israel; and you shall fall, you and all who are with you, and the nations that are with you shall be given as food to the multitude of birds, to all the birds of the sky; and to all the beasts of the field I have given you to be devoured.
Upon the face of the field you shall fall, for I have spoken, says Adonai the Lord.
And I will send fire upon Gog, and the coastlands shall be inhabited in peace, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
And my holy name shall be made known among my people Israel, and my holy name shall no longer be profaned, and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel.
Behold, it is coming, and you shall know that I am the Lord. This is the day of which I spoke.

And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel shall go out and shall kindle the weapons: shields and pikes and bows, and arrows and hand-staves and lances; and they shall kindle fire with them for seven years.

And they shall not bring wood from the field, nor kindle fire from the forests, but they shall burn the weapons with fire; and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and carry off their spoil, says Adonai the Lord.

And it shall be on that day, says the Lord, that I will give Gog a renowned place, a tomb in Israel, the Common Grave of those who come toward the sea; and they shall build around the mouth of that valley.
And there they shall bury Gog and all his multitude, and that place shall be called the Common Grave of Gog and of all his multitude.

And Israel shall bury him, so that the land may be cleansed in seven months; and all the people of the land shall bury him, and it shall be a renown for them on that day on which I shall be glorified, says the Lord.
And they shall continually send out men to survey the land, and to bury those left on the face of the land, and to cleanse it after seven months; and they shall search out
all who pass to and fro through the land; and whoever sees a human bone shall set up a sign beside it, so that the buriers may bury it in that place, the Common Grave of Gog.
For the name of the city also shall be Common Grave; and the land shall be cleansed.

And you, son of man, say: Thus says the Lord: Say to every winged bird and to every beast of the field: Gather together and come; gather from all around to this sacrifice of mine which I have slaughtered for you, a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel. Eat flesh and drink blood.
Eat the flesh of mighty men, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of calves and of goats, and of calves, all of them fattened.
And you shall eat flesh until you are full, and drink blood until you are drunk, from my sacrifices which I have slaughtered for you.
And you shall be filled at my table with horse and its rider, with the mighty man and every man of war, says the Lord.
And I will set my glory among you, and all the nations shall see my judgment which I have executed, and my hand which I have brought upon them.
And the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God from this day and henceforth.

And all the nations shall know that the house of Israel was led into captivity for their sins, because they acted with contempt toward me; and I turned my face away from them, and gave them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their lawlessness, and I turned my face away from them.
Therefore thus says Adonai the Lord: Now I will bring back the captives of Jacob, and I will have mercy on the house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
And they shall receive the shame and the lies by which they committed sin, when they dwell in peace in their own land, and there is no one to make them afraid.
This will be when I have brought them back from the nations and gathered them from the countries of the nations.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, when I appear to them among the nations
and I will no longer turn my face away from them, because I have poured out my wrath upon the house of Israel, says the Lord, the Lord.

Concerning the temple that was built. In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the tenth day of the month, in the fifteenth year after the city was captured, on that very day the hand of the Lord was upon me.
And in a vision of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, and on it there was something like the building of a city before it.
And he brought me into it, and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like shining bronze. In his hand were a builder's cord and a measuring reed, and he was standing at the gate.

And the man said to me, "Do you see this, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears, and set your heart on everything that I show you, for I have come in here in order to show it to you. And show all of this that you see to the house of Israel."

And I looked, and behold, there was a court outside the house, all the way around it. In the man's hand was a measuring reed six cubits long, by the cubit plus a span. He measured the outer wall: its width was one reed, and its height was one reed.
And he went into the gate that faces east, by seven steps, and he measured the porch (elam) of the gate: it was one reed.

And the chamber was one reed: its length was one reed and its width was one reed. The porch between the chambers was six cubits. The second chamber was one reed wide and one reed long, and the porch was five cubits.
And the third chamber was one reed wide and one reed long.

And the porch of the gate next to the porch of the inner gate was one reed. He measured the porch of the court at eight cubits, and the elev [?] (posts?) around it at two cubits, and the porches of the gate were on the inside.

And the chambers of the gate, the chambers at the front, were three on that side and three on this side. All three had one measurement, and the porches on that side and on this side had one measurement.
And he measured the width of the gate at ten cubits, and the breadth of the gate at thirteen cubits.
And at one cubit it narrowed in front of the face of the chambers, one cubit on this side and one cubit on that side. The chambers were six cubits on that side and six cubits on this side.
And he measured the gate from the wall of the chamber: its width was twenty-five cubits, and the same from gate to gate.
And the open-air part of the porch of the outer gate was twenty cubits, with the chambers of the gate all around.
And the distance from the uncovered part of the outer gate to the uncovered part of the porch of the inner gate was fifty cubits.

And there were hidden windows toward the chambers, forty [?], and toward the vestibule at the inner gate of the court, all around; and likewise all around the vestibule on the inner side. And toward the vestibule there were palm-trees on this side and on that.
And he brought me into the inner court, and behold, there were chambers, and columns all around the court: thirty chambers in the colonnade.
And there were porticoes on the south side of the gates, by the same measure as the gates, on the lower side beneath the colonnade.
And he measured the breadth of the court from the open space of the inner gate outward [?]; that is, to the open space of the gate that faces east. And he brought me toward the north.
And behold, there was a gate that faced north toward the inner court, and he measured its length and breadth.

And there were three chambers on this side and three on that, and pillars, and vestibules, and its palm-tree woodwork; and it was of the same measure as the gate that faces east: fifty cubits its length, and twenty-five cubits its breadth.
And its windows, and its vestibules, and the woodwork of its palm-trees were like those of the gate that faces east; and seven steps went up to it, and the vestibules were inside.
And there was a gate of the same kind on the inside, which faced opposite the north, like that of the gate which faced east; and he measured the court from gate to gate: a hundred cubits.
And he brought me toward the south, and behold, there was a gate that faced south; and he measured it, and its chamber, and pillar, and vestibule, by the same measure.
And its windows and vestibule all around were like the windows of the vestibule: fifty cubits its length, and twenty-five cubits its breadth.
And it had seven steps, and the vestibules were inside, and it had palm-tree woodwork, one on this side and one on that, toward the pillars.
And there was a gate opposite the gate of the inner court on the south side; and he measured the court from gate to gate: a hundred cubits; and the breadth on the south side, twenty cubits.
And he brought me into the innermost court, by the gate that faces south, and he measured the gate by the same measure.
And the chambers and pillars and vestibules were by the same measure, and it had windows and vestibules all around: fifty cubits its length, and twenty-five cubits its breadth.
And there was a vestibule at the inner gate, and palm-trees on the pillar, and eight steps.
And he brought me into the gate that faces east, and he measured it by the same measure.
And the chambers and pillars and vestibules were by the same measure, and it had windows and vestibules all around: fifty cubits its length, and twenty-five cubits its breadth.
And the vestibules were toward the outer court, and there were palm-trees toward the pillars on this side and on that, and it had eight steps.
And he brought me into the gate on the north side, and he measured it by the measure.
And its chambers, and pillars, and vestibules, and the windows all around it, and its vestibules: fifty cubits its length, and twenty-five cubits its breadth.
And the vestibules were toward the outer court, and there were palm-trees on its pillar on this side and on that, and it had eight steps.
Its chambers and its doors, and its vestibule at the second gate, and a drain,
so that they might slaughter there what is offered for sins and for sins of ignorance.

And on the south side of the outlet for the whole burnt offerings, which faces north, there were two tables toward the sunrise, and on the south side of the second, and of the porch of the gate, and eight tables on the east.
Four on that side and four on this side, on the south side of the gate; on them they slaughter the sacrifices of the whole burnt offerings, in front of the eight tables for the sacrifices.

And the four tables for the whole burnt offerings were of hewn stone, a cubit and a half in breadth, two cubits and a half in length, and one cubit in height. On them they set the vessels with which they slaughter the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices there.
And their rim [?] was one span, hewn as a ledge on the inside all the way around. And over the tables there was a roof as a covering against rain and heat.

And he brought me into the inner court, and behold, two chambers stood there in the inner court: one on the south side of the gate that faces north, and it runs toward the south; and one on the south of the gate on the south side, which faces toward the north.
And he said to me: "This chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep the charge of the temple.
And this chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who of the Levites draw near to the Lord to minister to him."
And he measured the court: a hundred cubits in length and a hundred cubits in breadth, on all four of its sides. And the altar was in front of the temple.
