And he brought me into the porch of the temple and measured the porch: five cubits of breadth on this side and five cubits of breadth on that side. The width of the doorway was fourteen cubits, and the side-walls of the door of the porch were ten cubits on this side.
And the porch was twenty cubits in length and twelve cubits in breadth, and they went up to it by ten steps. And there were pillars in the porch, one on this side and one on that side.
And he brought me into the temple and measured the porch: six cubits of breadth on this side and six cubits of breadth on that side,

and the width of the gate was ten cubits, and the side-walls of the gates were five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits.

And he went into the inner court and measured the porch of the doorway, two cubits, and its doors, six cubits, and the side-walls of the doorway, seven cubits on this side and seven cubits on that side.
And he measured the length of the doorway, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty, in front of the temple. And he said: "This is the Holy of Holies."
And he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits, and the breadth of its side-chambers, four cubits all around.

Side-chamber by side-chamber up to the next side-chamber, twenty-three, twice over. And there was a space left between the wall of the temple and the side-chambers all around, so that those who approached it could see, and so that they would not touch the wall of the temple at all.

And the breadth of the upper side-chambers increased with the wall upward all around the temple, so that it widened toward the top. And from the lower level they went up to the upper story, and from the middle ones to the third story.
And the [?] of the house, the height all around: the space between the side-chambers was equal to the reed, six cubits apart.
And the breadth of the outer side-chamber was five cubits, and the space left over between the side-chambers of the house.
And between the chambers was a space of twenty cubits, a passage going all around the temple.

And the doors of the seating-places of the chambers faced the remaining space: one door on the north side and one door on the south side. And the width of the open space of light of the remaining space was five cubits, the width all around.

And the dividing area in front of the remaining space was toward the sea (the west). In front of the house the length was a hundred cubits, and the remaining spaces, the area set apart and their walls were a hundred cubits in length.
And the width in front of the temple, together with the remaining space in front of it, was a hundred cubits.

And he measured the length of the dividing area in front of the remaining space at the back parts of the temple, and of the remaining space on this side and on that: a hundred cubits in length. And the temple, the side parts and the porch were joined on the outside.

And there were latticed windows to let in light all around the three, so that one could see in. And the temple and what was next to it were panelled with wood all around, both the floor and from the floor up to the windows. And the windows opened in three parts, so that one could see in.
And as far as the part next to the inner room and as far as the outside, on the whole wall all around, inside and outside,
cherubim and palm trees were carved, with a palm tree between each cherub and the next. Each cherub had two faces:
the face of a man turned toward the palm tree on one side and on the other, and the face of a lion turned toward the palm tree on one side and on the other. The whole temple was carved all around.
From the floor up to the ceiling there were carved cherubim and palm trees.
And the holy place and the temple opened out, four-cornered and [?], in front of the holy place. And its appearance was like the appearance

of a wooden altar. Its height was two cubits, its length three cubits and its width two cubits. It had horns standing up, and its base and its sides were of wood. And he said to me: "This is the table that stands before the Lord."
And the temple had two doors, and the holy place had two doors,
and the two doors were folding doors: two leaves for one door, and two leaves for the other door.

And there was carving on them: on the doors of the temple there were cherubim and palm trees, like the carving of the holy place. And there were sturdy [?] timbers in front of the porch on the outside.
And there were covered windows. And he measured the ceilings of the porch on this side and on that, and the sides of the temple were joined together.

And he brought me into the inner court from the east. He brought me in opposite the gates on the north side, and behold, there were five chambers next to the remaining space and next to the dividing area, on the north side.
They were a hundred cubits long toward the north and fifty cubits wide,
laid out like the gates of the inner court and like the colonnades of the outer court, arranged facing one another, as if in three tiers.
And in front of the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long on that side, and their doors were on the north side.

And the walkways of the upper rooms were the same, because the colonnade projected out from it, out from the lower parts of the colonnade, and was set apart. In the same way it was set apart from the colonnade, and so were the porticoes.
For it was in three tiers, and it had no columns like the columns of the chambers. That is why they projected out from the lower and the middle levels, from the ground.
And there was light outside, like the chambers of the outer court, which faced the chambers on the north side; the length was fifty cubits.
For the length of the chambers that faced the outer court was fifty cubits, and these face one another; and the whole was a hundred cubits.
And the doors of these chambers were on the eastern entrance, for going in from the outer court.
At the light at the beginning of the walkway, and on the south side, facing the south, and facing the remaining space, and facing the dividing space, and the halls of the dividing space.
They faced them, with the same measure as the chambers on the north side, with the same length and breadth, with all the same exits, all the same turnings, the same lights and the same doors.
Of the halls on the south side, and like the door at the beginning of the walkway, as toward the light, a space set apart by the measure of one reed; and people went in through them toward the east.

And he said to me: "These chambers on the north side and these chambers on the south side, which face the spaces set apart, are the halls of holiness. In them the priests, the sons of Zadok, who draw near to the Lord, shall eat. That is the holy of holies. There they shall lay the most holy things, and the sacrifices, and what is offered for sin, and what is offered for sins of ignorance, for the place is holy.

"No one shall enter there except the priests. They shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that those who come before the Lord may always be holy. And they shall not touch the garments in which they minister, for these are holy; they shall put on other garments when they go into the temple."
And he finished measuring the inner temple. Then he brought me out by way of the gate that faces east, and he measured the appearance and plan of the temple all around, in its arrangement.
And he stood on the south side of the gate that faces east, and measured five hundred with the measuring reed.
And he turned to the north side, and measured on the north side five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
And he turned toward the sea, and measured on that side of the temple five hundred.
And he turned to the south, and measured on that side of the temple five hundred with the measuring reed.

He measured all four sides with the same reed and laid them out. There was a wall all around it, five hundred cubits on the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to separate the holy places from what lay in front of the wall, according to the arrangement of the temple.
And he brought me toward the east side, which the place faced, and led me outside.

And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was coming by the way of the east side. The sound of his camp was like the sound [?] of a great multitude redoubled, and the earth all around shone like light from his glory.

And the vision that I saw was like the vision I saw when I went in to anoint the city. The appearance of the revelation that I saw was like the vision I saw at the river Chebar. And I fell on my face.
And the glory of the Lord entered the temple by way of the gate that faces east.
And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and behold, the temple was full of the glory of the Lord.
And I stood, and behold, there was a voice from inside the temple, and it spoke to me; and the man was standing near me.

And he said to me, “Have you seen, son of man, the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where my holy name dwells in the midst of the house of Israel forever? From now on the house of Israel shall not defile my holy name, neither they nor their princes, by their fornication and by the murders of their leaders among them,

by setting their doors before my gateways and my thresholds next to their thresholds. They made my wall as though it were joined to me and to them, and they defiled my holy name by the lawless deeds that they committed. I will crush them in my anger and with slaughter.
And now let them put their fornications and the murders of their princes far away from before me, and I will dwell among them forever.
And you, son of man, show this temple of mine to the house of Israel, so that they may cease from their sins, and show them its appearance and its arrangement.

And they shall bear their punishment for all the deeds that they have done. And you shall portray this house to them, and its exits, and its structure, and all its ordinances. Make all its law known to them, and portray it before them, so that they may keep all my judgments and all my ordinances and do them.
And the plan of the house is on the summit of the mountain, and all its boundaries round about are the holy of holies.

And these are the measurements of the altar in cubits, a cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the hollow is a cubit deep and one cubit wide, and the rim around its edges is one span. And this is the height of the altar:

from the depth of its hollow up to the great ledge (literally “propitiatory”) on the lower part, two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the small ledge to the great ledge, four cubits, and the width one cubit.
And the ariel (the altar hearth) is four cubits, and from the ariel up to the horns above, one cubit.
And the ariel is twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on all four of its sides.

And the ledge (literally “propitiatory”) is fourteen cubits wide, square toward its [?]. Its rim all the way around is half a cubit, and its surround is one cubit on the outside; and its steps faced toward the east.

And he said to me, “Son of man, thus says the Lord God of Israel: These are the ordinances for the altar on the day it is made, for offering whole burnt offerings on it and for sprinkling blood on it.
And you shall give to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who draw near to me to minister to me, says the Lord God, a calf from the herd as a sin offering.

And they shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge (literally “propitiatory”), and on the base all around; they shall make atonement for it.
And they shall take the calf that is for the sin offering and burn it in a separate place of the temple, outside the holy places.
And on the second day they shall take two kids from the goats, without blemish, for sin, and they shall make atonement for the place of atonement, as they made atonement with the calf.
And after the atonement is completed, you shall offer a calf from the cattle without blemish, and a ram from the sheep without blemish.
And you shall offer them before the Lord, and the priests shall pour salt on it, and they shall offer it to the Lord as a whole burnt offering.
For seven days you shall offer a kid for sin, day by day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep, without blemish, shall be offered
for seven days. And they shall make atonement for the altar and purify it, and they shall fill their hands.

And from the eighth day onward, the priests shall offer your whole burnt offerings on the altar of your whole burnt offerings, and the offerings for your well-being, and I will accept you, says Adonai the Lord.
And he brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the holy places, which faces east; and it was shut.
And the Lord said to me: This gate shall be shut and shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it, for the Lord God of Israel shall enter by it, and it shall be shut.
For the prince shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate, and he shall go out by the same way.
And he brought me in by the way that faces north, in front of the temple, and I looked, and behold, the house of the Lord was full of the glory of the Lord. And I fell on my face.

And the Lord said to me: Son of man, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I speak to you, according to all the ordinances of the house of the Lord and according to all its laws. And set your heart on the entrance of the house, according to all its exits among all the holy places.
And say to the rebellious house, the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Let it be enough for you of all your iniquities, O house of Israel!

You brought in the sons of foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and in flesh, to be in my holy places, and they profaned them when you offered bread, flesh and blood, and you transgressed my law with all your iniquities.
And you appointed guards to keep watch in my holy places.

Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: No one born a foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter my sanctuary, none of those born of foreigners who are among the house of Israel.
But the Levites, who turned away from me when Israel went astray from me to follow their own thoughts, shall bear their falsehoods.

And they shall be in my holy places as servants and as doorkeepers at the gates of my house. These shall serve the house, and they shall slaughter the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices of the people, and they shall stand before the people to serve them;
because they served them before their idols, and it became for the house of Israel a punishment of falsehood. Therefore I lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God.

And they shall not come near me to serve me as priests, nor to offer the holy things of the sons of Israel, nor to approach my holy of holies. And they shall bear their disgrace for the error in which they went astray.
And they shall appoint them to keep the charge of the house, in all its work and in all that is done in it.

The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my holy things when the house of Israel went astray from me: these shall come near to serve me, and they shall stand before me to offer me sacrifice, the fat and the blood, says the Lord God.
These shall enter my holy places, and these shall come near to my table for my service, and to keep my charges.
And when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall put on linen garments. They shall not put on wool while they serve at the gate of the inner court.
A linen headdress [?] shall cover their heads, and linen breeches shall be on their loins. They shall not put them on tightly.

And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they served and lay them in the chamber of the holy places. They shall put on other garments, so that they do not make the people holy with their garments.
They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not bare their hair; they shall keep their heads covered.
And no priest shall drink wine when they enter the inner court.
And they shall not take a widow or a divorced woman as a wife for themselves, but only a virgin of the race of Israel. If the widow is the widow of a priest, he may marry her.
And they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the profane, and make known to them the difference between the clean and the unclean.

And in cases of bloodshed they shall stand to judge. They shall uphold my ordinances and judge by my judgments. They shall keep my law and my commandments at all my feasts, and they shall keep my sabbaths holy.

And they shall not go near the body of a dead person, so that they are not defiled. But for a father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or a sister of his who has not yet had a husband, they may go near and be defiled.
And after his cleansing, seven days shall be counted for him.
And on the day that they enter the inner court to minister in the sanctuary, they shall offer a sin offering of atonement, says the Lord God.
And they shall have no inheritance. I will be their inheritance. And no land shall be given to them among the sons of Israel; I am the land of their inheritance.
And they shall eat the offerings and the sacrifices made for sin and for ignorance. And everything set apart and vowed in Israel shall be theirs.

The first fruits of everything, and the firstborn, and every offering from all your first fruits shall belong to the priests. Give your first fruits to the priest, so that your blessing may rest on your houses.
And the priests shall not eat anything, bird or beast, that has died by itself or has been torn by animals.

And when you divide the land as an inheritance, you shall set apart for the Lord a holy portion of the land as first fruits, twenty-five thousand cubits long and twenty thousand wide. It shall be holy within all its borders round about.
Of this, a square of five hundred by five hundred cubits all around shall be for the sanctuary, with an open space of fifty cubits all around it.
And by this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of twenty thousand. In it shall be the Holy of Holies.
This portion of the land shall belong to the priests who minister in the sanctuary and who come near to the Lord to serve him. It shall be a place for their houses, set apart as holy for them.
twenty-five thousand in length and twenty thousand in breadth, and for the Levites who serve the temple of God, for them to hold cities as their possession.
For the city's holding you shall give five thousand in breadth and twenty-five thousand in length, alongside the first-fruits of the holy portion; it shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

And for the prince: on this side and on that side of the first-fruits of the holy portion and of the city's possession, in front of the first-fruits of the holy portion and in front of the city's possession, toward the sea, and from the sea toward the east; its length shall be like one of the portions, from the boundaries on the sea side, and its length to the boundary on the east side of the land.
And it shall be their possession in Israel, and the princes of Israel shall no longer oppress my people, and the sons of Israel shall possess the land, tribe by tribe.
Thus says the Lord God: Enough of this, you princes of Israel! Put away falsehood and misery, and do judgment and righteousness, and take away oppression from my people, says the Lord God.
You shall have a just balance, a just measure and a just kabits [a dry measure] as your measures.
And the kabits shall be one and the same for receiving and for giving: the kabits is a tenth of a homer, and a tenth of a homer; it shall be measured equally by the homer.
And the weight shall be twenty-five obols; fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
And this is the first-fruits that you shall set apart: a measure from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of it, a measure from thirty grivi [a dry measure] of barley.
And the ordinance for oil: ten gverdi [a liquid measure] from a hundred gverdi, and one gverdi from ten gverdi, for ten gverdi make a gomor.
And one sheep out of ten sheep as an offering from all the tribes of Israel, for sacrifices, for whole burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to make atonement for you, says the Lord God.
And all the people shall give the first-fruits to the prince of Israel,

and it shall be the prince's duty to provide the whole burnt offerings, the sacrifices, and the offerings for the feasts, the new moons, the Sabbaths and all the feasts of the house of Israel. He himself shall make the offering for sin, and the offering, the whole burnt offerings and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take an unblemished calf from the herd to make atonement for the sanctuary.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the atonement and smear it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the temple, on the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
And he shall do the same in the seventh month, on the first day of the month: he shall take an offering from each person and make atonement for the house.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, which is the feast of the passion. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
And the prince shall make an offering for himself, for his house and for all the people of the land: one calf for sin.

And during the seven days of the feast he shall make whole burnt offerings to the Lord: seven young bulls and seven unblemished rams, every day for the seven days; and a kid of the goats for sin every day, and an offering.
Baked bread with the calf, and baked bread with the ram, and six xestes of oil with the baked bread.
And in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at the feast, you shall do the same for seven days: as for the sin offering, and as for the grain offering, and as for the oil.

Thus says the Lord God: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut on the six working days, but it shall be opened on the sabbath day, and it shall be opened on the day of the new moon.
And the prince shall enter by way of the vestibule (elam) of the outer gate and stand before the doors of the gate. The priests shall offer his whole burnt offerings and his peace offerings.

And he shall worship before the doors of the court, and the priest shall come out. The gate shall not be shut until evening. And the people shall worship before the Lord before the doors of the court on sabbaths and new moons.
And the whole burnt offering that the prince shall offer to the Lord on the sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and one ram without blemish.
And there shall be a grain offering, a cake with the ram and with the lambs, an offering given as the gift of his hand, and a measure of six xestes of oil with the cake.
And on the days of the new moons there shall be a bull calf without blemish, six lambs, and a ram without blemish.
And there shall be a cake with the ram and a cake with the calf as a grain offering, and for the lambs as much as his hand can afford, and a measure of six xestes of oil with the cake.
And when the prince enters, he shall enter by way of the vestibule (elam) of the gate, and he shall go out by way of the same gate.

And when the people of the land come in before the Lord at the feasts, whoever enters by way of the north to worship shall go out by way of the [?] gate, and whoever enters by way of the south gate shall go out by way of the north gate. He shall not turn back again to the gate by which he entered, but shall go out straight ahead, opposite it.
And the prince shall be in their midst: when they enter, he shall enter with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.
At the feasts and assemblies there shall be a grain offering: a cake with the calf, a cake with the ram, and for the ten lambs as much as his hand can afford, and six xestes of oil with the cake.

If the prince offers to the Lord a whole burnt offering of thanksgiving (confession) or a peace offering, the gate that faces east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his whole burnt offerings and his peace offerings as he does on the sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and after he has gone out the door shall be shut.
He shall offer a year-old lamb without blemish to the Lord as a whole burnt offering every day; he shall offer it in the morning.

And with it in the morning he shall make a grain offering of a sixth of a measure, and a third of a measure of oil, two xestes, to mix with the wheat flour as a grain offering to the Lord. This is an ordinance forever.
You shall offer the lamb, and you shall offer the grain offering and the oil in the morning, and a whole burnt offering continually.
Thus says the Lord God: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it shall belong to his sons, and they shall hold it as their inheritance.
If he gives a gift to one of his servants, it shall be the servant's until the year of release, and then it shall return to the prince. Only the inheritance of his sons shall remain theirs.

And the prince shall not take anything from the inheritance of the people so as to oppress them. Instead, he shall give his sons their inheritance from his own land, so that my people are not scattered, each one from his own inheritance.
And he brought me in at the entrance of the gate on the south side, to the seat of the holy priests, which faces north, and there was a place set apart there.

And he said to me: "This is the place where the priests boil the offering for ignorance and for sin. There they also bake the grain offering (manna), so that they do not carry it out into the outer court and make the people holy."
And he brought me out into the outer court, and led me around to all four corners of the court.

And behold, there was a court [?] at the corner of the court, a court at each corner, at all four corners of the court. Each was a small court, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; all four had the same measurements.
And there were kitchens built underneath the [?] all around.
And he said to me: "These are the kitchen-houses, where the ministers of the temple boil the sacrifices of the people."

And he brought me in before the door of the temple, and behold, water was coming out from beneath the open porch [?] on the east side. The water was flowing down from the right side, from the south, toward the altar.
And he brought me out by way of the north gate, and led me around by the outer way to the gate of the court that faces east; and behold, the waters were flowing down from the right side.
Like a man going out straight ahead, he had a measuring line in his hand. He measured a thousand with that measure, and he went through the water: water of release.
And he measured a thousand, and he went through the water, water up to the thighs [?]. And he measured a thousand, and he went through the water up to the waist.
And he could no longer cross over, because the water was rising like the rush of a torrent that cannot be crossed.
And he said to me: "Have you seen this, son of man?" And he brought me to the bank of the river.
When I turned back, behold, on the bank of the river there were very many trees on both sides.
And he said to me: "This water goes out toward Galilee in the east, and was flowing down into Arabia, and was coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outflow, and it will make the waters live.

And every living creature that comes forth, wherever the river reaches, shall live, and there shall be very many fish there, for this water comes and heals. All that this river reaches shall be saved and shall live.
And fishermen shall stand there; from Engedi [?] there shall be a place for drying nets, and there shall be fish of the Great Sea in very great numbers.
But its outflow and its rising [?] shall not be healed; they are given over to salt.

And on the river, along its banks on both sides, every tree for food shall spring up. Its leaves shall not wither, and its fruit shall not fail; it shall bring forth the first fruits of its newness, because their waters come out from the sanctuary. Their fruit shall be for food, and what springs up from them for life.
Thus says the Lord God: "These are the borders of the land that you shall give as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel, an added portion of measure."
And you shall inherit it, each man like his brother, concerning which I lifted up my hand to give it to their fathers; and this land shall be to you an inheritance by allotment.
These are the boundaries of the land on the north side: from the Great Sea, which comes down and divides the entrance of Hamath, Eldaama,
Bethar, Ebrem, Eliam, between the borders of Damascus and between the borders of Hamath, the courts of Saunan, which are above the borders of the Hauranites.
These are the boundaries from the sea, by the court of Saunan, by the border of Damascus, and to the north.

And toward the east: between the Hauranites and Damascus, and between the Gileadites and the land of Israel, the Jordan is the boundary to the sea, on the east side of the Palm Grove [?]; this is toward the east.
And on the south side and the north: from Teman and the Palm Grove [?] as far as the water of Arimoth of Kadesh, it extends as far as the Great Sea.
This is the region on the south and on the north. These regions of the Great Sea form the boundary as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, up to its entrance; this is the sea side of Hamath.
And you shall divide this land for them, tribe by tribe, to Israel.

You shall divide it for them by lot, for yourselves and for the sojourners who dwell among you, who have begotten children among you. They shall be to you like the native holders of the land among the sons of Israel; they shall eat with you in the inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And they shall be in the tribe, among the sojourners who were with them; there you shall give them their inheritance, says the Lord God.

And these are the names of the tribes, beginning from the north side, by the region along the descent which divides the entrance of Hamath, the court of Aunan [?], the border of Damascus to the north, by Hamath beside the court. They shall have from the east as far as the sea: Dan, one portion.
And from the border of Asher, from the east as far as the sea: Naphtali, one portion.
And from the border of Naphtali, from the east as far as the sea: Ephr[?]
And from the border of Manasseh, from the east as far as the sea: Ephraim, one portion.
And from the border of Ephraim, from the east as far as the sea: Reuben, one portion.
And from the border of Reuben, from the east as far as the sea: Judah, one portion.

And from the border of Judah, from the east as far as the sea, there shall be the firstfruits set apart, twenty-five thousand in breadth, and in length like one of the portions, from the east as far as the sea; and the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it.
The firstfruits which they shall set apart for the Lord: in length twenty-five thousand.

This shall be the firstfruits of the holy things for the priests: toward the north twenty-five thousand, toward the sea ten thousand, and toward the south twenty-five thousand; and the mountain of the holy things shall be in the midst of it.
It is for the sanctified priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the watches of the house, who did not go astray in the straying of the sons of Israel, as the Levites went astray.
And they shall have firstfruits from the given firstfruits of the land, a holy of holies, from the borders of the Levites.
And for the other Levites, next to the borders of the priests: in length twenty-five thousand and in breadth ten thousand; the whole length twenty-five thousand, and the breadth twenty thousand.
None of it shall be sold, nor shall it be measured off; the firstfruits of the land shall not be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.

And the remaining five thousand of space beyond the twenty-five thousand shall be an outer wall (literally "the wall of the wall") of the city, for dwelling and for its open land. The city shall be in the midst of them.

And this is its measure: on the east five hundred and four thousand, on the south five hundred and four thousand, on the north four thousand five hundred, and on the side of the sea four thousand five hundred.
And there shall be land set apart for the city: on the north side one hundred and fifty, on the east one hundred and fifty, and on the side of the sea one hundred and fifty.

And the rest of the length, next to the first-fruits of the holy things, shall be ten thousand on the east and ten thousand toward the sea. These shall be the first-fruits of the holy place, and its produce shall be bread for those who work for the city.
And those who work for the city shall work it, from all the tribes of Israel.
All the first-fruits shall be twenty-five thousand, four-square. You shall set it apart as the first-fruits of holiness, separate from the possession of the city.

And the rest shall belong to the prince, on this side and on that side of the first-fruits of the holy things and of the holding of the city. It shall be twenty-five thousand in length, as far as the borders on the side of the sea, next to the borders of the prince. It shall be the first-fruits of the holy things, and the sanctuary of the house shall be in its midst.
Apart from the Levites' portion and the possession of the city, which lie among the princes' portion, the land between the borders of Judah and the borders of Benjamin shall belong to the princes.
And of the remaining tribes: from the east as far as toward the sea, Benjamin, one portion.
And from the border of Benjamin, from the east as far as toward the sea, Simeon, one portion.
And from the borders of Simeon, from the east as far as toward the sea, Issachar, one portion.
And from the borders of Issachar, from the east as far as toward the sea, Zebulun, one portion.
And from the borders of Zebulun, from the east as far as toward the sea, Gad, one portion.

This is the land which you shall divide as portions for the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
And these are the exits of the city: on the north side, four thousand five hundred by measure.
And the gates of the city shall bear the names of the tribes of Israel. There shall be three gates on the north: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; and the gate of Levi, one.
And on the east, four thousand five hundred, with three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; and the gate of Dan, one.
And on the south, four thousand five hundred, with three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; and the gate of Zebulun, one.
And on the side of the sea, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
